product.headline: Game localization, all in one place.
product.description: From source files to AI translation, review and export. A desktop workspace for game and mod localization, with consistent terminology, tone and source updates.
product.destination: Packages, supported environments and update information are available on IkumyonTools.
product.screen: Edit source text, translations and translation states side by side
product.translate.title: Translate. Review. Refine.
product.translate.body: Translate with AI, review the results and edit the details yourself. Manage multiple target languages and export Paradox YAML or ParaTranz JSON.
product.update.title: When the source changes, keep going.
product.update.body: Detect updates in source folders and review additions, changes and deletions before importing. Carry existing translations forward and revisit what changed.
product.compare.title: Keep the voice. Choose the words.
product.compare.body: Use glossaries and tone settings to guide each project's language. Compare translations from multiple models and choose the version that fits the context.
product.start.title: Start with your first translation.
product.start.body: Get the package from IkumyonTools, extract it and launch. The user guide walks you through setup and your first translation.
product.ai: AI features require an API key or authentication depending on the connection. Each service has its own pricing and terms.
guide.splash.title: Change the startup splash image
guide.splash.setup: Create a splash folder beside the launcher and place images directly inside, then start the launcher. Supported extensions are png, jpg, jpeg, webp and bmp, case-insensitively. Subfolders are not searched. No Settings registration is needed. With multiple images, one is randomly selected at each launch.
guide.splash.display: The window adapts to the image within a logical width of 480–900 and height of 260–650. The image covers the window, so edges may be cropped depending on its aspect ratio. The application name and progress overlay the image, with a dark gradient at the bottom. Keep important text and details away from the edges and bottom.
guide.splash.check: If no image appears, check the splash folder beside the launcher, the extension and whether the image opens. Only when that folder is absent does the launcher search splash in the working directory. No supported image or failure to load the selected image results in the default startup screen. It does not retry another image during that launch: remove damaged files and restart the launcher. Starting the Python application directly does not show this launcher screen.
pluginDev.title: Creating a plugin
pluginDev.description: Create a Python plugin and try installing it and exporting translation text.
pluginDev.choose.title: 1. Choose a capability and implementation
pluginDev.choose.body: Python plugins can add file formats (parser), AI connections (provider), exporters, glossary_formats, voice_input, operations and ui. Try the exporter below in the host development environment first. Python runs in the host process and needs dependencies available to that process. The executable kind implements file formats and exporters in a separate process.
pluginDev.files.title: 2. Create the folder and manifest
pluginDev.files.body: Create plugins/example_text/ in the application root and place manifest.json and entry.py inside it. The root is the repository root during development, or the executable directory in a distribution (its parent if the executable is inside core). Save the following as manifest.json. Choose an id unique across built-in and external plugins. name, version and description describe the plugin in the inventory. kind defaults to python and entry to entry.py. entry must be a relative path inside the plugin folder.
pluginDev.example.title: 3. Implement entry.py
pluginDev.example.body: Save the code below as entry.py. During register(context), call context.register() exactly once with a PluginContribution whose id matches; at least one capability is required. An exporter provides id, name, exchange and plan(), returning ExportFile objects with relative paths and bytes. The host writes the files. exchange=False receives output text selected and prepared by the host. This learning example joins translations with newlines; it does not preserve keys, states or the original file structure.
pluginDev.verify.title: 4. Verify loading and export
pluginDev.verify.body: Restart the application and open a translation project. Loading succeeds if Example text (*.txt) appears among export formats. This example registers no settings page, so it has no dedicated entry under Settings → Plugins. Choose an empty output folder, languages and translation states, export, and inspect 1.txt (2.txt and later for multiple inputs). Untranslated items, empty translations and items outside the selected states use source text. If loading fails, check startup logs for JSON syntax, entry location, duplicate IDs and import errors. Restart after changes.
pluginDev.extend.title: 5. Add settings and UI
pluginDev.extend.body: Read and write private settings with context.settings.load() / save(dict). Register a SettingsPageProvider in UIContribution.settings_pages with id, title, create_widget(parent) and save_settings(widget). Define static widgets and layout in .ui files; load them and connect events in Python. Use context.ui_language, on_language_changed() and on_close() for language and cleanup. notify_display_changed() requests a host display refresh.
pluginDev.references.title: 6. File format and export API
pluginDev.references.body: The signatures below list required members; implement the ellipses. Import types from autolingua2.plugins.contracts. The parser id must match the plugin. Provide at least one GameProfile(id, name, slots, default_slot_id); slots contains GameSlot(slot_id, name, language_code). The default slot is empty when there are no slots, otherwise a declared slot ID. List extensions in suffixes, such as {".txt"}; default_filter_rules may be empty. can_load tests support, filter_source_files selects input files, detect_source_language returns a language code or None, and load returns ImportedTranslation. Fill project.sources, project.units and source_refs mapping each unit ID to SourceRef(source_id, external_id). For exporters, exchange=True receives original records; False receives translation or source text according to selected states. ExportFile paths must be relative within the destination; absolute paths, .., duplicates and overwriting existing files are rejected.
pluginDev.rpc.title: 7. Executable manifest and protocol
pluginDev.rpc.body: The manifest below uses windows and linux as OS keys. Place executables inside the plugin folder and specify relative paths and arguments. Each call starts a new process with that folder as its working directory. Read one UTF-8 JSON line from stdin. Write newline-terminated JSON with version: 1 and the received request id to stdout, then exit with code 0. Optional progress messages precede exactly one final result or error. The four envelope examples show request, progress, success and failure; never send both success and failure. Send diagnostic logs to stderr. Each line is limited to 64 MiB; timeouts are 30 seconds for register and 600 seconds otherwise. The method examples show params and result. Replace absolute paths with actual OS paths and echo the received id. load must return exactly one source whose id is the loaded absolute path; source_refs keys must exactly match unit IDs. export_plan returns file bytes as Base64 in content_base64; the example encodes UTF-8 text.
pluginDev.manifest:
{
  "id": "example_text",
  "name": "Example text export",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "kind": "python",
  "entry": "entry.py",
  "description": "Export selected translation text as UTF-8"
}
pluginDev.code:
from pathlib import Path
from autolingua2.plugins.api import PluginContext, PluginContribution
from autolingua2.plugins.contracts import ExportFile, ImportedTranslation


class TextExporter:
    id = "text"
    name = "Example text (*.txt)"
    exchange = False

    def plan(self, workspaces: list[ImportedTranslation],
             settings: dict[str, object]) -> list[ExportFile]:
        outputs = []
        for index, imported in enumerate(workspaces, start=1):
            lines = [unit.target_text for unit in imported.project.units]
            content = ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
            outputs.append(ExportFile(Path(f"{index}.txt"), content))
        return outputs


def register(context: PluginContext) -> None:
    context.register(PluginContribution(
        id=context.id, exporters=[TextExporter()],
    ))

details.triggers.title: Automatic execution with triggers
details.triggers.description: Learn how to invoke a processing .als at app startup, project opening, translation completion or a specified time. This covers registration, syntax checking, execution confirmation and logs.
details.triggers.overview: Triggers monitor events and conditions, then ask for confirmation to run a processing script when they match. Screen operations themselves are written in a separate .als. Scheduled times are effective while the app is running; they do not run processing while it is closed or replay missed times after sleep.
details.triggers.prepare.title: Prepare the processing script first
details.triggers.prepare.body: On the automation screen's Processing tab, save the desired operations as an .als. The trigger body defines the event and conditions, and run specifies that file. Put screen-click and input commands in the processing .als. Even correct trigger syntax cannot execute processing if the invoked file does not exist.
details.triggers.prepare.test: Before registration, run the processing script manually and verify that it works with the intended project and screen. Moving or renaming the file requires updating run, so save it in a stable location. Triggers require an absolute .als path; relative paths and other file formats are not accepted.
details.triggers.register.title: Add and save a trigger
details.triggers.register.body: Open the Triggers tab on the automation screen and press Add. Select the target in the list and enter a descriptive name and trigger body. Insert path… lets you choose a processing .als and insert its quoted path. Check how to write it with Syntax help, and use Check syntax to look for errors.
details.triggers.register.save: Press Save and apply after editing. A syntax check alone does not save edits. Use the list checkbox to enable or disable the trigger and check that its state is Enabled / Listening. Switching to another trigger with unsaved edits shows a save confirmation; choose whether to save or discard them.
details.triggers.events.title: Choose the event that starts processing
details.triggers.events.body: app_started means app startup, project_opened means opening a project, and translation_completed means translation completion. Project information is available as project.is_open, project.name, project.source_language and project.target_language. Add conditions such as the intended project being open or the target language matching before calling run.
details.triggers.events.schedule: A time such as schedule("09:00") is checked daily while the app is running. Missed times are not replayed when the app was closed or resumes from sleep. Startup events do not fire again merely when you save a registration; to test startup behavior, save and restart the app.
details.triggers.example.title: Example: invoke processing after Japanese translation finishes
details.triggers.example.body: The following example invokes a processing script after translation completes only if a project is open and its target language is ja. D:/scripts/after-translation.als is an example; replace it with the absolute path of your saved processing file.
details.triggers.example.explain: This body determines when and which file to invoke. Write the actual checking, saving and other operations in after-translation.als. For multiple languages, check whether the current target is an appropriate condition. For a daily morning run, change the event to on schedule("09:00") while retaining the necessary project conditions.
details.triggers.confirm.title: Read the confirmation and run
details.triggers.confirm.body: A matching event waits for execution confirmation. Check the displayed trigger, event and processing file, then choose Run or Cancel. Registration does not make all operations continue without confirmation. After switching projects, also check that the execution target has not changed.
details.triggers.confirm.wait: Execution confirmation may wait during translation, loading or another modal screen. The same trigger does not queue duplicate requests while waiting for confirmation or running. If confirmation does not appear immediately, first check ongoing processing and open dialogs.
details.triggers.logs.title: Check logs and processing results
details.triggers.logs.body: Trigger logs record pending confirmations, cancellations and loading or evaluation errors. Once processing starts, check status and logs on the Processing tab too. Distinguish failure to evaluate trigger conditions, failure to read the file and failure in screen operations in the invoked script.
details.triggers.logs.errors: If nothing happens, check the enabled checkbox, saved body, event name, time, conditions and absolute .als path in order. 'No syntax problems' does not guarantee file existence or successful operation on the actual screen. Run the same processing file manually before invoking it from a trigger to isolate the cause.
details.triggers.disable.title: Disabling, deleting and repeated execution
details.triggers.disable.body: Clear the list checkbox to stop using a trigger temporarily. To remove its definition, verify the target and use Delete. If processing has already started, disabling alone does not undo completed changes. Also check Stop on the Processing tab and processing results.
details.triggers.disable.loop: Project-opened and translation-completed events arising during automation or trigger processing may be ignored to avoid recursive execution. Do not build a workflow assuming a translation started by one trigger will chain into another trigger of the same kind when complete. Write consecutive operations in order within the processing script.
details.mcpServer.description: Configure a connection so external tools on the same computer can request project reading, editing, translation and export. Also learn which operations to expose and how to check results.
details.mcpServer.overview: Enabling the app's MCP connection lets external tools connect to the running app. Choose exposed operations from read, edit, translate and export, then register the URL and connection token with the external tool. Check the app's proposals and processing results as well as the external conversation while working.
details.mcpServer.prepare.title: Decide connection direction and exposed operations
details.mcpServer.prepare.body: Here the external tool makes requests and this app is the operation target. This is the opposite direction from providing external resources to AI Chat. Open the target project and decide what the external tool should do before opening MCP settings. The target is the app on the same computer, so closing it makes the connection unavailable.
details.mcpServer.prepare.permissions: Expose read for investigation only, edit to change translations and other data, and the corresponding operations for translation or export. If a required operation is not exposed, a successful connection still cannot execute that request. Choose exposed operations according to what you want the external tool to handle.
details.mcpServer.example.title: Try reading before making changes
details.mcpServer.example.body: After registering connection information in the external tool, first request the current project name or target language to verify that it connects to the intended app. Then narrow investigations to specific item IDs or files to make the operation target clear. You do not need to request changes to every item just to test the connection.
details.mcpServer.example.change: For example, after requesting 'Find inconsistent terminology in this file and propose changes', compare the proposals displayed in the app's AI Chat. In Review proposals mode, select and apply only the items you want. In Execute as requested mode, changes happen directly, so check the operation scope and execution method beforehand. Afterwards, check results in the app and save the project.
details.mcpServer.errors.title: Connection problems and changed settings
details.mcpServer.errors.body: If connection fails, check that the app is running, MCP is enabled and the connection status shows a URL after Apply. Also check that the external tool supports Streamable HTTP and has the correct URL and credentials. Make sure you did not register only the URL while omitting Authorization information.
details.mcpServer.errors.token: Changing the port or connection token invalidates the old information stored by external tools. Apply the settings, use Copy connection information to obtain the new details and update the external tool too. Even if you stop the external conversation, check in the app whether started translations or exports are still running.
details.mcpResources.description: Register a local-process or HTTP MCP connection, test it and use resources so AI Chat can consult external reference material.
details.mcpResources.overview: External resource connections let this app read MCP resource lists, templates and contents. Follow the provider's instructions to register an executable or URL and test the connection. Registration does not make every operation of that external MCP available in AI Chat.
details.mcpResources.prepare.title: Prepare a provider of resources
details.mcpResources.prepare.body: Prepare the MCP endpoint publishing the resources you want and its connection method. It must support resource listing and reading resource contents. An MCP that only offers operation tools may not work as a resource connection. Before registration, check which resources the endpoint provides.
details.mcpResources.prepare.types: Choose Local process to launch a program on your computer to read resources, or HTTP to connect to a running MCP URL. Required executables, arguments, URLs and credentials vary by provider. Do not register a resource folder or ordinary web page URL directly as an MCP endpoint.
details.mcpResources.local.title: Check input for each connection method
details.mcpResources.local.body: For Local process, enter the executable and launch arguments separately. Arguments are one per line; do not paste the entire command as a single argument. Match the executable location and resource-selection arguments to the provider's procedure. If the connection test fails, first check program location and argument separation.
details.mcpResources.http.body: For HTTP, specify the HTTP or HTTPS URL accepting MCP connections. This may differ from the resource viewing or administration page URL. Provide a connection token if authentication is required. After changing URLs or credentials, test before saving to verify resources can be read.
details.mcpResources.use.title: Find and consult resources in AI Chat
details.mcpResources.use.body: After a successful connection test and saving settings, return to AI Chat and explain which resources to use and why. For example, request 'Find examples of this proper noun in registered resources and compare them with the current translation.' Specifying the term or item to check, rather than just 'Look at the resources', helps connect relevant references with translation items.
details.mcpResources.use.verify: In the answer, check the wording found in resources and the scope of translations proposed for change. Reading resources and modifying glossaries or translations are separate processes. To adopt findings, request the necessary changes or apply them manually, then check the proposals and save the project.
details.mcpResources.maintain.title: Change or remove connections
details.mcpResources.maintain.body: Select a registered connection and use Edit to change its name or connection information. Delete unused connections and press Apply or Save. If an external executable moves or a server URL or token changes, update the registration and test the connection again.
details.mcpResources.errors: If connection fails, check the method, executable or MCP URL, arguments, token and endpoint availability. If connection succeeds but resources are missing, check that the MCP supports resource listing and reading and publishes the requested resources. Changing the app's incoming MCP enable setting will not fix an external resource connection.
details.automation.results.title: Check results and save your work
details.automation.results.body: Check script completion, trigger logs and results of MCP-requested processing on their respective screens. Command acceptance or successful connection alone does not mean translation or export succeeded. Review changed translations and glossaries, then save content that should remain in the project.
details.automation.results.stop: Stopping does not undo completed operations. Stopping the initiating conversation or script is also different from cancelling translation or export that has already started. Check app progress and processing results before rerunning to avoid duplicating partly completed operations.
details.support.title: Troubleshooting and app updates
details.support.description: Learn how to isolate causes using the problem list and processing results, what to check for connection, translation and export issues, and how to update the app.
details.support.first.title: Identify the stage that stopped
details.support.first.body: First check the operation performed, target project and language, and displayed message. File loading, AI connection, translation, proofreading, saving and export involve different settings. If you recently changed settings, also verify that those changes were applied or saved.
details.support.first.save: If on-screen edits are unconfirmed, distinguish them from confirmed translations. Save the project if possible, read the error, then review settings and targets. Narrowing down to a few items that reproduce the issue makes failure conditions easier to identify than repeatedly translating or exporting everything without knowing the cause.
details.support.problems.body: Use type, target, description and filename as clues in the problem list. Filter by filename, search for the target key or source, and inspect it in list or focus view. Item problems and the latest AI communication error may appear in different places, so check translation states and processing results too. A displayed problem does not mean every translation failed.
details.support.connection.title: Cannot connect to AI or select a model
details.support.connection.body: On the AI settings page, check authentication and the model list for the provider you use. If authentication expired, review sign-in or the API key; for model-name problems, inspect the error on that row. After a successful connection test, save settings and check model selections for translation and AI Chat too.
details.support.connection.models: If only some models fail, investigate their registered names and availability rather than the whole provider. If translation cannot start after deleting a model, review high, low and proofreading model assignments. For communication or usage-limit errors, use the message to decide when and what to retry.
details.support.translation.title: Translation does not run or cannot be found
details.support.translation.body: Check target language, target selection, search and status filters, exclusion and lock states. If translated items seem to disappear from the list, check whether you are showing only Untranslated. Switch to All and search for the key or source to find translated items too.
details.support.translation.review: If translation succeeds but proofreading errors occur, check the proofreading model and results. If glossary or tone settings are not reflected, check the current target's selections and whether you retranslated after changing definitions. Existing translations may be inherited after a source update, so also review Source updated / Needs review.
details.support.export.title: Cannot export or output differs from expectations
details.support.export.body: Check that target languages have been added, the output destination exists and there are no duplicate filenames or destinations. Translation export is not restricted to selected languages or rows. For multiple languages, check output slot collisions too. Cancellation or failure can leave generated files behind, so check the destination before rerunning.
details.support.export.state: If source text is exported instead of translations, check unconfirmed edits and Translation statuses to use. Some formats use source text for excluded states or empty translations. ParaTranz JSON handles state selection differently; check the format-specific explanation. Thumbnail export has a separate menu; check PNG/JPEG and .mod settings there.
details.support.update.title: Check for app updates
details.support.update.body: Open Help → Check for updates…. If an update is available, check current and latest versions, release date, download size and release notes. Choose Later if you do not want to update now. If no update is available, the installed version is displayed; close the screen and continue working.
details.support.update.install: Save unsaved projects before updating. Choosing the download operation starts the updater and closes the main app. Follow the updater's instructions afterwards. Merely checking for updates does not start installation.
details.support.update.errors: If the update check fails, read the details and use Retry to check again. An updater-not-found message means the app distribution needs to include that executable. Distinguish communication errors from missing executable files. An error does not mean you are on the latest version; distinguish it from a successful check.
details.tone.conditions.body: Prepare the normal tones to switch between before creating a conditional tone. Then configure the condition target, matching content and normal tone to use. For example, to handle dialogue and description files separately, build conditions after checking actual file information and target items. For advanced conditions, follow the condition expression specification displayed on screen.
details.tone.conditions.check: After creating conditions, test both items that should match and items that should not. If the resulting tone differs from expectations, check the selected tone on the main screen, condition target, condition value and referenced normal tone in order. Selecting a conditional tone does not mean every item matches its conditions.
details.tone.verify.title: Check translations after changing definitions
details.tone.verify.body: Editing a tone does not automatically update previous translations. Retranslate the items that should reflect the new instructions and check both terminology and tone. When confirming a translation manually, select the normal tone applied to it. For multiple languages, check each language's selection and save the project at the end.
details.yaml.title: Exporting Paradox YAML
details.yaml.description: Learn how to configure language slots, folder layout and EU4 encoding for game YAML output and check the generated results.
details.yaml.overview: Paradox YAML contains translation files for the game to load. Check not only the target language but also the output slot, folder layout and encoding suitable for the game. Some items revert to source text depending on selected translation states, so assess output settings together with translation review status.
details.yaml.prepare.title: Check target languages and language slots
details.yaml.prepare.body: For each output language, check the translation states to use and the output slot. Even if the translation is Japanese, the language slot used in the game may be another language. Output slots affect YAML headers and filenames, so match the actual game installation rather than judging only by the text's language.
details.yaml.slot.example: If multiple targets are configured, switch to each language and check its settings. Assigning different translations to the same output slot can produce identical output destinations. All languages are exported, so do not finish after checking only the currently selected language.
details.yaml.layout.title: Choose the folder layout for your installation
details.yaml.layout.body: With language folders, folders corresponding to output slots are created under localisation or localization in the destination. A same-folder layout omits this intervening language folder. Check both the generated top-level folder and subfolders inherited from the source, and place them where the game or mod expects them.
details.yaml.encoding.check: EU4 CJK escape changes how exported text is represented. Do not judge only by its appearance in a text editor; check display in the game environment using that method. If text becomes garbled, check the combination of export method, installed files and environment. Do not apply EU4 settings unchanged to other games.
details.yaml.verify.title: Check generated files and in-game display
details.yaml.verify.body: After export, check that files exist for the expected languages, along with their language suffixes, headers and folder structure. Choose representative keys and check items using translations as well as those reverting to source because of state selection. After installation, check the displayed text and make sure color, variable and other tags remain intact.
details.yaml.errors: For duplicate filenames or destinations, review the destination folder and each language's output slot. If export succeeds but changes do not appear in the game, check file placement and the language slot loaded by the game. If source appears instead of translations, first check confirmation state and Translation statuses to use.
details.json.title: Exchanging ParaTranz JSON
details.json.description: Learn the data structure, state mapping and import/export checks for exchanging translation items through ParaTranz JSON.
details.json.overview: ParaTranz JSON exports source text, translation, key, context and translation state. Unlike game YAML, it does not replace translations with source text based on Translation statuses to use. Check how app states map to ParaTranz states before continuing work at the receiving end.
details.json.workflow.title: Decide how to exchange translation items
details.json.workflow.body: ParaTranz JSON exchanges texts to be translated. Do not confuse it with glossary JSON. Confirm pending edits and save the project before exporting. Choose ParaTranz JSON in Export translations… and transfer the files generated in each language's folder. Export is not restricted to the rows filtered by search.
details.json.workflow.import: Handle received translation files through Add source files or the import step in project creation. Exporting JSON alone does not synchronize later changes back into an existing project. If using translation inheritance, check keys and target languages and distinguish this from importing the same content as a separate project.
details.json.example.title: Check state conversion with examples
details.json.example.body: For example, both AI translations and human translations become stage 1 in ParaTranz. AI proofreading and human proofreading become stage 3. The transferred state alone cannot tell you whether the original translation was produced by AI or a person. Retain the original .alproj if you need to distinguish that work history.
details.json.example.loss: Questionable items and items with proofreading findings are both grouped into stage 2. Do not treat ParaTranz stage 5, meaning a second review is complete, as equivalent to stage 3 exported by this app for proofread items. A round trip may not preserve every distinction because the formats represent states at different levels of detail.
details.json.verify.title: Check keys, translations and states before transfer
details.json.verify.body: Inspect representative generated JSON items and check that key, original, translation, context and stage are as intended. With multiple source files or target languages, check the folder-to-language mapping too. An empty translation in an untranslated item does not by itself mean export failed: this format does not substitute the source text.
details.json.glossary: If you want to transfer a bilingual term list, use glossary import/export instead of this output screen. Translation lists and glossaries serve different purposes and have different JSON structures. If filenames do not make the distinction clear, check which format was used before transferring them.
details.bmfont.title: Character lists for BMFont
details.bmfont.description: Learn how to collect characters from source text or output translations and generate text for selecting characters when building a font.
details.bmfont.overview: A character list collects the unique characters used in text. Choose either source text or translations with selected states taken into account. It does not generate a font or font atlas; use the exported list in your font creation tool.
details.bmfont.purpose.title: What a character list can do
details.bmfont.purpose.body: Use this when building a game font containing only the required characters. Instead of manually picking characters from sources and translations, collect them from project text. Duplicates are removed, so each character occurs only once in the list regardless of its frequency in the text. Characters are ordered by Unicode, not first occurrence.
details.bmfont.prepare: The list reflects text currently stored in the project. If source updates have not been applied or translations remain unconfirmed, it may not match the text used later. Finalize sources and translations consistently with translation-file export before generating the character list.
details.bmfont.selection.title: Choose source or translation characters
details.bmfont.selection.body: Choose Source under Target text to collect source characters. If you choose Translation, also check which translation states are used. Items outside the selected states or with empty translations use the source, so even a translation character list can include characters found only in the source.
details.bmfont.selection.example: For example, even a list intended for Japanese translations includes English letters if untranslated items retain English source text. Selecting only confirmed translations causes unreviewed items to revert to source, so the list may not contain every required Japanese character. Match state selection to the same text you plan to export as game YAML.
details.bmfont.use.title: Use generated files to select characters
details.bmfont.use.body: Open characters.txt, characters_language.txt or characters_source.txt as appropriate and treat them as UTF-8 text. Import the list into your font creation tool or use its contents to select characters. Font selection, size, atlas placement and font definition file generation are performed in that tool.
details.bmfont.verify: For multiple languages, verify the mapping between output slots used in filenames and languages. Adding or editing text can require new characters, so regenerate the list when finalizing translation files for release. A character appearing in the list does not guarantee the chosen font has its glyph; check that separately.
details.ai.title: AI connections and model settings
details.ai.description: Follow authentication, model registration, connection testing and model assignment for translation and proofreading. Use the same procedure to change providers or models after initial setup.
details.ai.overview: Using AI requires provider authentication, registration of models to use and selection of models for actual translation. A model that passes a connection test is not necessarily assigned automatically to every purpose. After changing providers, check high, low and proofreading model selections as well.
details.ai.prepare.title: Check authentication and model selection separately
details.ai.prepare.body: Open Settings → Translation → AI. Authentication enables access to a provider; model settings choose what to use at that provider. Models are also assigned to translation and AI Chat. When a problem occurs, check which stages are complete: authentication, registration and assignment to a purpose.
details.ai.prepare.auth: For ChatGPT, sign in through the browser; for API providers, configure the appropriate API key. Select the intended provider before entering credentials to avoid mixing up services. Even if connected during initial setup, check the model list and connection test again after signing out or changing credentials.
details.ai.models.title: Register models and test the connection
details.ai.models.body: Check the model list after authentication. Where refresh or add controls are available, register the models you want and enable their rows. Match model names to those accepted by the provider. Entering a name does not by itself make that model available to your account. Disable or remove unwanted candidates to keep the list focused on models you use.
details.ai.models.test: Run Connection test and check the available count and errors. Read errors on failed rows and correct credentials or model names. If only some fail, distinguish successful models from failed ones. After success, press Apply or Save to apply settings. Testing and saving settings are separate operations too.
details.ai.assign.title: Assign models to translation and proofreading
details.ai.assign.body: After registering accessible models, choose high and low models in Translation settings. If using AI proofreading after translation, configure the proofreading model too. Check the main screen's AI settings panel for the intended models, glossary and tone. After deleting or changing a provider, check whether previous assignments are still usable.
details.ai.assign.example: Just after adding a provider, try translation and proofreading on a few items first. If translation succeeds but proofreading fails, check the proofreading model assignment. Check AI Chat model selection separately from translation model settings. Even when using the same model for each purpose, verify each selection field has the intended setting.
details.ai.verify.title: Verify changes with actual processing
details.ai.verify.body: Save settings, return to the main screen, select the target language and translate representative items. If your work includes long text or tags, test such sources too. After successful translation, try proofreading as needed, inspect the results and state changes, and save the project.
details.ai.errors: For authentication errors, check provider sign-in or API keys; for model-not-found errors, check registration names and access rights; for missing-model errors before translation, check purpose assignments. Even after a successful connection test, later processing can encounter usage limits or communication errors. Read the displayed error before reviewing the relevant settings.
details.plugins.title: Check plugins
details.plugins.body: Plugins add AI providers, file formats and game-specific settings. Check the required features under Plugins in Settings. If game-specific output settings are missing, first check the project's game, format and relevant plugin. Not every project shows the same additional settings.
details.plugins.check: After changing plugin state, check guidance or errors on the settings screen. For AI provider changes, review model settings and connection tests; for file-format changes, review import and export methods. Being able to close settings does not by itself mean the feature is fully prepared.
details.settings.files: Configure source folder monitoring together with source update import. The saved project's source and the current external source are managed separately, so detecting differences and applying them remain necessary after enabling monitoring. The project management child page covers registration through post-update checks.
details.settings.mcp: MCP provides connections for external tools to operate this app and for this app to read external resources. Although both are in MCP settings, their directions and purposes differ; configure the one you need. Automation and external integration explains registration and checking results.
details.automation.workflow.title: Choose an execution method for your purpose
details.automation.workflow.body: Use scripts for repeated screen operations and triggers to invoke processing at startup or when translation completes. Configure an MCP connection to the app for external AI tools to read and operate on projects, or an external resource connection for AI Chat to read reference material. Choose operation automation and resource access separately.
details.automation.workflow.example: For example, to add the same target language repeatedly, first write a processing script and verify it manually. To run the same check after translation, register that script with a trigger. To have external AI find inconsistent terms, expose the app's MCP read and edit operations as needed, then review and apply proposals.
details.scripts.title: Creating and running scripts
details.scripts.description: Learn how to create .als files, inspect screen target IDs and automate repeated work while checking execution results and errors.
details.scripts.overview: Scripts operate the screen by executing commands in order. First organize the manual procedure and check the target screens and IDs, then create a short process. The runner waits for dialogs, translations and saves to complete, so you normally do not need to guess wait times and insert them between commands.
details.scripts.prepare.title: Define the procedure and starting screen
details.scripts.prepare.body: Break your intended process into its starting screen, selections, inputs and results to check. For processing that requires a project, prepare the target project and language first. A button's enabled state depends on the screen state, so do not omit prerequisite operations.
details.scripts.prepare.ids: When specifying buttons or input fields, inspect the actual target IDs on screen. A displayed Japanese label is not necessarily the operation ID. Check the target and verify one operation before adding the next to make wrong-screen and wrong-ID problems easier to identify.
details.scripts.example.title: Adapt examples to your environment
details.scripts.example.body: For the add-language example, check the language code to add and the project open at the start. The screen differs depending on whether that language is already added. Do not just change the example string and execute everything at once; verify the operations required on your screen in order.
details.scripts.example.files: Saved .als files can be loaded again with Open. Give them descriptive names, and save them somewhere stable if a trigger will invoke them. Saving a script preserves its instructions; it does not save the project changed by that script. Include a save operation at the end if needed.
details.scripts.debug.title: Investigate using line/column numbers and screen state
details.scripts.debug.body: On errors, check the status and log line and column numbers, then read the corresponding command. Compare it with the actual screen: the target may be missing, disabled or in a dialog that is not open. If translation or saving fails, check the processing failure reason as well as command syntax.
details.scripts.debug.retry: Operations completed before stopping or failure remain in place. Before rerunning, check whether languages have already been added or inputs partly completed, then restore the expected starting state or revise the procedure to continue from there. Manual operations during execution also stop it; wait for completion before interacting with the screen to inspect it.
details.updates.title: Source updates and folder monitoring
details.updates.description: Learn how to detect source changes, review additions, modifications and deletions, and import them into an ongoing translation project.
details.updates.overview: When following updates to a game or mod, check the source update feature before recreating the project. Register the original folder for monitoring, review detected differences and import them. You can retain translations with the same item IDs while reviewing items whose source text changed. Deciding to apply an update and checking each language's translations afterwards are separate tasks.
details.updates.workflow.title: Understand the workflow before importing updates
details.updates.workflow.body: Opening an .alproj alone does not replace its source text with the latest files at the import location. The project stores the source text from the time of import. Its source is updated when folder monitoring detects changes, prepares differences, and you review and apply them. Before working, check the current target and number of languages, and save under another name if you want to retain the current state.
details.updates.example: For example, if a mod update adds ten dialogue entries and changes two descriptions, you need to translate the new dialogue and review the existing translations of the changed descriptions. A changed item may retain its translation, but that translation may no longer match the new content. Even if only the context changed, check whether the speaker or scene has changed.
details.updates.register.title: Register monitoring targets and check detection
details.updates.register.body: Open Settings → Files → Source folder monitoring and use Add to register the source that is actually updated. Check the folder location and target information so you do not confuse the project's output destination with its import source. Enable Start monitoring and check the monitoring status and number of registered targets. Registering, editing or deleting targets and starting or stopping monitoring are saved when you perform those operations. Registered targets cannot detect updates while monitoring is stopped.
details.updates.register.check: If expected changes do not appear, first check the target folder and error count. Review the registration if you moved the monitored target or the original game or mod is unavailable. Detecting and applying updates are different operations. If an update is pending, open its review screen and compare additions, changes and deletions.
details.updates.after.title: Check each language after applying updates
details.updates.after.body: After applying an update, check added items with Untranslated first, then changed items with Source updated / Needs review to separate the work. If you have multiple targets, finishing one language's review does not finish the others. Switch target languages, check the glossary and tone, translate and proofread, then save your work in the project.
details.updates.errors: If the source changes again while the review screen is open, you may not be able to apply the initially displayed differences. Retrieve the new differences and review them again. Check whether deleted items are truly no longer needed by the game. Monitoring errors and item translation errors have different causes, so investigate monitoring details and individual item states separately.
details.thumbnail.title: Editing and exporting thumbnails
details.thumbnail.description: Learn how to edit a project thumbnail with image and text layers and export it as PNG or JPEG. This also covers canvas and layer resizing, transparency and mod image references.
details.thumbnail.overview: You can edit the project's image by layering multiple images and text. Image position, size and rotation are configured separately from the canvas that defines the final image bounds. After applying the edited image to the project, use Export thumbnail… to write a PNG or JPEG as needed. This is separate from exporting translation files.
details.thumbnail.open.title: Prepare an image and open the editor
details.thumbnail.open.body: Specify the image to use on the project creation screen. Drop an image or add one through the file picker, then hover over its preview and press Edit. In the thumbnail image editor, check the base image and final image bounds. Edit is unavailable until an image is set, so add the original image first.
details.thumbnail.open.example: To add a Japanese edition label to a mod title image, retain the original as the background and add text above it. Decide the aspect ratio required for your purpose before resizing the entire original image to avoid repeatedly repositioning the text. Preview zoom controls visibility and is independent of exported image dimensions.
details.thumbnail.layers.title: Add and select image layers
details.thumbnail.layers.body: Add material with Image… and select the layer to edit. Move adjusts the selected material's position. When materials overlap, select the intended one in the layer list before operating to avoid moving the background accidentally. Added images are composited onto the canvas; portions outside the canvas are excluded from the final image.
details.thumbnail.layers.order: Layer stacking order can hide text or images behind other material. If an element is positioned correctly but invisible, check both the visible bounds and stacking order. Verify the selected target before deleting an unwanted layer. Keeping the background and heading on separate layers lets you enlarge only the text or move only the background.
details.thumbnail.transform.title: Adjust position, size and rotation
details.thumbnail.transform.body: Adjust the selected layer using movement X and Y, scaling width and height, and rotation angle. Numeric values help align material sizes and positions. Enable Lock aspect ratio when changing dimensions to retain proportions. Positive rotation angles turn clockwise and negative angles counterclockwise; 90-degree buttons are also available. Alignment places material at the left, right, top, bottom or center of the canvas.
details.thumbnail.transform.interpolatio: Interpolation determines how pixels are filled during scaling. Compare nearest neighbor for pixel art whose edges you want to preserve, and bilinear, bicubic or Lanczos for photos and smooth images. After zooming in to inspect, check readability at the actual display size too. Changing interpolation cannot restore details absent from the original image.
details.thumbnail.canvas.title: Choose between resizing the canvas and cropping
details.thumbnail.canvas.body: Resize canvas changes the final image's width and height and which part of the image falls within its bounds. Adjust width, height and horizontal and vertical alignment, inspect the preview, then press Apply resize. This differs from scaling a layer; choose the operation according to whether you want more margins or larger material.
details.thumbnail.canvas.crop: To remove unwanted surroundings, specify the area to retain with Crop, confirm it, then check that text and logos are not cut off. Press Escape to cancel while defining the area. For easier viewing, use Ctrl and the mouse wheel to zoom, and Space with left drag or middle-button drag to pan. These viewing operations do not change final image dimensions.
details.thumbnail.text.title: Add text and make it readable
details.thumbnail.text.body: Select Text, choose an insertion point on the canvas and enter the text. Select existing text with the text tool to edit it. Adjust the content, font and size, and check readability over the image. Text is also an independent layer, so you can adjust its position, size, rotation and alignment after adding it.
details.thumbnail.text.example: For a label such as 'Japanese translation', first place it over an area with little background detail and size it so it does not hide the title or logo. Check that it is readable both enlarged in the editor and when the final image is shown small. A short label at a sufficient size is easier to check than thin text or a long passage crammed into the image.
details.thumbnail.apply.title: Apply the edits and save the project
details.thumbnail.apply.body: Check the final bounds, layer positions and text, then press Apply in the editor. Verify that the image preview on the creation screen is as intended, then create and save the project using that image. Confirming the editor, saving work in an .alproj and exporting PNG or JPEG are three separate operations.
details.thumbnail.apply.reset: Reset all returns to the single original image from when the editor was opened, clearing added layers and edits. After Apply, the image is carried forward as a flattened composite. Reopening Edit does not let you edit the previous text or added images as separate layers, so check text errors and positioning before applying.
details.thumbnail.export.title: Choose PNG or JPEG export settings
details.thumbnail.export.body: Open File → Export thumbnail… and specify the destination, filename and format. Export is unavailable if no thumbnail is set. If a file already exists, an overwrite confirmation appears; verify the target before proceeding. Image export does not filter by translation item status or target language.
details.thumbnail.export.png: Use PNG to preserve transparency or the edges of text and logos. Compression level ranges from 0 to 9 and adjusts compression strength without changing quality. When Optimize compression is enabled, optimization determines compression and the compression level field is unavailable. Choose settings while checking file size and processing time.
details.thumbnail.export.jpeg: For JPEG, select Quality from 1 to 100. Chroma subsampling offers 4:4:4, 4:2:2 and 4:2:0; compare 4:4:4 to retain fine color boundaries and 4:2:0 to reduce size. Progressive saving and Optimize compression are also available. JPEG cannot preserve transparency, so choose the fill color under Background color for transparent areas.
details.thumbnail.metadata.title: Check metadata and mod image references
details.thumbnail.metadata.body: Preserve metadata retains image information that the export process can carry over. This is separate from the image's appearance and export format. If you need specific information, check the exported file too. Not all configured information is necessarily saved identically in PNG and JPEG.
details.thumbnail.mod.body: For Paradox output, you can select Update image reference in .mod. If enabled, specify the .mod file to update using Browse… or the equivalent control. Check that the initially displayed descriptor.mod is the intended file. This setting changes the mod's image reference as well as saving the image, so clear it when you only want to export an image.
details.thumbnail.export.check: After export, open the saved image and check its dimensions, transparency or background color, and clipped text. If you chose to update .mod, also check that the target file references the correct image name. Correct destination or .mod errors before running the export again.
details.dashboard.title: View progress by language on the dashboard
details.dashboard.body: Switch to the overview from View to see the project name, source language, file count, source item count and progress for each target language. Use this screen to identify which languages still need translation or review before reading text in the list. File count and source item count differ: one file can contain multiple translation items.
details.dashboard.languages: Language rows show translation progress, untranslated, confirmed, needs review and other counts. Selecting a row also changes the active translation target. If you resume translating after viewing another language's progress, check the target, glossary and tone on the main screen. Add language lets you prepare another target.
details.dashboard.states: A table and chart show counts and percentages by state for the selected language. Click a table state or chart segment to select it and inspect its breakdown. Select the same state again to clear the selection. Chart selection is for checking progress; it does not confirm translations or change translation states.
details.dashboard.example: Even if translation progress is high, review any remaining Needs review items before exporting for publication. After a source update, also watch the Source updated / Needs review count, and switch to list or focus view to inspect the text. Distinguish the number translated by AI from the number reviewed by a person.
details.translation.compare: The comparison screen displays results for each registered, enabled model. If one model fails, distinguish its error from the other results. Compare terminology consistency, missing source information and whether the tone fits the scene. If short proper nouns make differences hard to judge, try items with context as well.
details.translation.adopt: After pressing Adopt this translation for the desired result, return to the main screen and check the translation. Edit it as needed, confirm the translation and save the project. This feature does not take a majority vote between models: even if several results share an expression, assess correctness against the source.
details.glossary.workflow.title: From registration to use in translation
details.glossary.workflow.body: Glossaries standardize the relationship between source terms and specified translations; tones standardize writing style. First check the game and source and target languages, create the definitions, then select the glossary and tone in the main screen's AI settings. Registration alone does not automatically apply them to every project or target language.
details.glossary.workflow.example: For several mods of the same game, put shared place names and titles in a parent glossary and mod-specific names in child glossaries. To use plain style for descriptions and character-appropriate tones for dialogue, prepare normal tone definitions separately from the conditions that select them. Translate a few items first to verify your instructions work as intended and reduce the need to redo everything.
details.glossaryEditor.title: Creating, editing and inheriting glossaries
details.glossaryEditor.description: Learn how to register source terms, translations and variants, and inherit a shared glossary for different works or mods.
details.glossaryEditor.overview: Create a glossary and register source and target terms to standardize wording. Variants and case sensitivity affect source matching, so configure them while checking the actual source. Use parent-child relationships to manage shared and specific terms separately. Changes are saved immediately; do not edit assuming Cancel in settings will undo them.
details.glossaryEditor.example.title: Register expressions as they appear in the source
details.glossaryEditor.example.body: For example, when registering 'Royal Guard' as the representative source expression and '近衛隊' as its translation, check the spelling actually used in descriptions and dialogue. Register terms at the level you want to standardize, and note distinctions between common words and proper nouns to make later review easier. Set fields such as part of speech according to the term's role.
details.glossaryEditor.example.variants: If plurals or alternative spellings are used, register them as variants to expand matching. Case-sensitive settings may prevent a match when the source capitalization differs. Broad matching, on the other hand, can also pick up common words with the same spelling. After registration, search for source text containing the term and translate a few items to check that the specified translation is used.
details.glossaryEditor.inheritance.title: Separate shared and specific terms using parent and child glossaries
details.glossaryEditor.inheritance.body: Register game-wide place names and titles in the parent and mod-specific character or organization names in children to manage shared content without duplicating it. When adapting a term in a child, distinguish terms inherited from the parent from definitions owned by the child. Parent changes affect inheriting glossaries too, so avoid changing a shared specified translation solely to suit one project.
details.glossaryEditor.check: After editing, check the selected glossary and target language, then translate representative items. Updating a glossary does not replace all already-confirmed translations. To standardize existing translations too, find the relevant items with search and retranslate or edit them manually. Checking registrations and applying them to existing translations are separate tasks.
details.glossaryExchange.title: Importing and exporting glossaries
details.glossaryExchange.description: Learn how to merge glossary JSON into an existing glossary or import it as a new one, export parent-child relationships, and exchange ParaTranz glossaries.
details.glossaryExchange.overview: Import and export glossary JSON in the glossary manager. This is different data from ParaTranz JSON used to exchange translation items. Check the format and destination before importing, then choose whether to merge into an existing definition or create a new glossary. Export options also differ depending on whether you want to preserve hierarchy or provide inherited terms together.
details.glossaryExchange.prepare.title: Check format, languages and import destination
details.glossaryExchange.prepare.body: Before importing, check that the file contains glossary JSON rather than a translation list. In the glossary manager, check the game, source-term language and translation language, and choose the import target. For externally created JSON, set Format to match the file type. A .json extension does not mean all files can be read in the same format.
details.glossaryExchange.choose: Use a merge into the selected glossary to build on existing terms, or create a new glossary to compare it as a separate candidate. For hierarchical data, choose an import method that preserves its structure. Imports are saved immediately, so export the required glossaries first if you want to retain their previous contents.
details.glossaryExchange.merge.title: Understand what a merge changes
details.glossaryExchange.merge.body: If a term already exists in the glossary, merge behavior depends on the format. The AUTOlingua2 format updates information in both languages; external formats merge expressions and notes while retaining existing representative expressions and other information. Do not assume every existing translation will be replaced with the imported value; read the screen's explanation before proceeding.
details.glossaryExchange.verify: After completion, check counts of created, added and updated entries and search representative terms. Verify that source and target have not been reversed, variants were added as expected and existing specified translations were retained. Check results after each file: continuing to merge into the wrong destination makes the cause harder to trace.
details.glossaryExchange.example.title: Transfer a glossary to another environment
details.glossaryExchange.example.body: Choose the AUTOlingua2 format including structure for a recipient who will edit parent-child relationships. To provide the complete terms available in a specific child glossary, choose an export that includes inherited parent terms. For ParaTranz, use its glossary format and check which settings it cannot represent and therefore omits.
details.glossaryExchange.errors: If import fails, check whether you selected translation-file JSON, chose the wrong format or tried merging hierarchical data into an existing glossary. Exporting to another format and back may not preserve all information, such as variants and hierarchy. Choose the format based on the information needed by the recipient.
details.tone.title: Normal and conditional tones
details.tone.description: Learn how to define translation writing instructions as normal tones and select them according to conditions such as source text and files.
details.tone.overview: Normal tones define writing instructions such as plain style or polite guidance. Conditional tones choose a normal tone that matches their conditions. Managing specified term translations separately from overall writing style lets you change the tone between dialogue and descriptions while sharing a glossary.
details.tone.instructions.title: Write specific tone instructions
details.tone.instructions.body: A tone name identifies it in the selection list; the instruction prompt contains what the AI receives. Specify necessary features such as sentence endings, politeness level and first-person pronouns. Contradictory instructions can make results inconsistent, so start with short instructions and adjust them while testing representative source text. Keeping specified proper-noun translations in the glossary makes tone instructions easier to read.
details.tone.instructions.example: For descriptions, specify something like 'Translate in plain Japanese da/de aru style. Preserve the meaning of the description and avoid excessive honorific language.' For dialogue, add the speaker's necessary characteristics without having the AI invent details absent from the source. Do not consider the instructions finished just from reading them; test short sentences, long sentences, questions and other source examples.
