setup.overview.body: The setup wizard opens automatically the first time you start Autolingua Desktop.
setup.overview.note: You can change all settings later. To get started quickly, skip setup with Set up later.
setup.displayLanguage.title: 1. Choose a display language
setup.displayLanguage.description: Choose the language used in the app's menus and dialogs.
setup.displayLanguage.selection.label: Display language
setup.displayLanguage.selection.body: Choose a language from the list. System default follows your operating system's language setting.
setup.displayLanguage.custom.label: Create a new language with your own translation
setup.displayLanguage.custom.body: Select this if your language is missing or you want to create your own translation dictionary. A UI translation screen will appear after AI setup.
setup.displayLanguage.next: Choose a language, then click Next in the lower right.
setup.aiSelection.title: 2. Choose an AI
setup.aiSelection.description: Choose the AI service (provider) to use for translation.
setup.aiSelection.openai.label: OpenAI
setup.aiSelection.openai.body: Use GPT models with an OpenAI API key.
setup.aiSelection.google.label: Google Gemini
setup.aiSelection.google.body: Models such as Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Gemini 3 Pro.
setup.aiSelection.anthropic.label: Anthropic Claude
setup.aiSelection.anthropic.body: Models such as Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5.
setup.aiSelection.plugins.label: Other plugins
setup.aiSelection.plugins.body: Additional external providers and local LLMs.
setup.aiSelection.next: Select a provider and click Next.
setup.aiConnection.title: 3. Configure your AI and test the connection
setup.aiConnection.description: Sign in or enter an API key for the selected AI, check the models, and test the connection.
setup.aiConnection.key.label: Enter an API key
setup.aiConnection.key.body: For Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, or OpenAI, enter the service's API key. It is filled in automatically if an environment variable is available. ChatGPT sign-in does not require an API key.
setup.aiConnection.models.label: Check the models
setup.aiConnection.models.body: Check or add model names. Reset to default models restores the recommended defaults.
setup.aiConnection.test.label: Connection test
setup.aiConnection.test.body: Click Connection test and confirm that all selected models are available.
setup.aiConnection.note: Next and Finish remain disabled until connection testing has completed for all enabled models.
setup.uiTranslation.title: 4. Translate the app interface (optional)
setup.uiTranslation.condition: This step appears only if you selected Create a new language with your own translation in step 1.
setup.uiTranslation.ai.label: Translate with AI (recommended)
setup.uiTranslation.ai.body: Use the AI configured in step 3 to translate missing interface text. The app installs the QM dictionary and switches languages automatically.
setup.uiTranslation.ts.label: Export a TS file to translate yourself
setup.uiTranslation.ts.body: Save untranslated text as a .ts file to translate with a tool such as Qt Linguist.
setup.navigation.title: Navigation buttons
setup.navigation.back.label: Back
setup.navigation.back.body: Return to the previous step to change your language or AI selection.
setup.navigation.next.label: Next
setup.navigation.next.body: Confirm your entries and continue. Enabled after a successful connection test where required.
setup.navigation.finish.label: Finish
setup.navigation.finish.body: Save your settings, finish setup, and open the main window.
setup.navigation.skip.label: Set up later
setup.navigation.skip.body: Skip AI setup. Only your language selection is saved.
setup.skipAndReset.title: Skip setup or change settings later
setup.skipAndReset.body: Even if you skip setup with Set up later or Esc, you can configure it later in Settings from the main window, under Language and AI.
firstTranslation.title: Your First Translation
firstTranslation.description: Follow the steps from importing source text to AI translation, review, project saving, and translation export.
firstTranslation.before.title: Before you start
firstTranslation.before.body: Prepare the files or folder you want to translate. This example translates English source text into Japanese. Available formats and games depend on the plugins you use.
firstTranslation.before.models: AI translation requires AI configuration. If you skipped setup, enter your credentials and register models under Settings → AI, then choose the High model and Low model under Translation. Also select a review model if you want AI review after translation.
firstTranslation.create.title: 1. Create a project from source text
firstTranslation.create.body: On Create project, select a Game and enter a Project name. Specify an Output folder (optional) if needed.
firstTranslation.create.source.label: Add source text
firstTranslation.create.source.body: On the Source tab, choose the Source language and drop the files or folder onto the screen. You can also use Add files or Add folder. If a file filter is shown, select the appropriate source files and check the added sources.
firstTranslation.create.inherit.label: If you already have translations (optional)
firstTranslation.create.inherit.body: After adding sources, use the Inherit translations tab to add existing translation files or folders. Check the Target language and import status. Specify the target language when inheriting translations embedded in source ParaTranz JSON as well. Skip this step if you are creating translations for the first time.
firstTranslation.create.next: Check the settings, click Create project, and wait for parsing to finish. If an import error appears, check the selected game, format, and source files.
firstTranslation.language.title: 2. Add a target language
firstTranslation.language.body: After opening the project, click + Add language. Search for Japanese in the language list, click Add on its row, then Close. Confirm that Target language in the main window is correct. Inherited languages can also be selected there.
firstTranslation.language.note: Translations and statuses are managed in a separate workspace for each target language. If an Output slot is shown, also check the language slot in the output file. Target language and output slot are separate settings.
firstTranslation.translate.title: 3. Translate with AI
firstTranslation.translate.body: Confirm that the target language is Japanese, then click ▶ Translate all at the top. Untranslated entries in the current target language are translated in order. If the button says ▶ Translate selected (count), clear the row selection first.
firstTranslation.translate.selected.body: Select rows to change the top button to ▶ Translate selected (count), then click it. If your selection includes translated entries, choose whether to overwrite them or translate only untranslated entries in the confirmation dialog.
firstTranslation.translate.all.label: What Translate all includes
firstTranslation.translate.all.body: It includes untranslated entries with nonempty source text. Search and status filters do not limit it to visible rows. Existing translations are kept.
firstTranslation.translate.note: Progress appears at the bottom. When the success and failure counts are displayed, review the translations. If an AI configuration warning appears, check the indicated models or credentials and try again. For failed entries, check the settings and error, select those rows, and retry.
firstTranslation.review.title: 4. Review and edit translations
firstTranslation.review.body: Compare the source and translation. Focus view lets you review entries individually and use AI translation for the current entry. Edit the translation as needed.
firstTranslation.review.save: Confirm edited translations using options such as Save as human translation or Save as human review in the Save menu. Save and next (human translation) confirms the entry and moves to the next one. If an unconfirmed marker is shown, make sure to confirm your edits.
firstTranslation.review.filter: The initial status filter is Untranslated. If translated rows disappear, switch to All or AI translated to see them.
firstTranslation.save.title: 5. Save the project
firstTranslation.save.body: Choose Save project and specify a location and filename. Work is saved as an .alproj file. Open this project to resume later. Remember to save the project after confirming individual translations too.
firstTranslation.export.title: 6. Export translation files
firstTranslation.export.body: Open Export translations and select the Output folder and Export method. Check the statuses to include and the selected method's export settings, then click Export. Check the output files before using them in your game or tool.
firstTranslation.export.note: Saving a project and exporting translations are separate operations. To use AI translations in formats such as Paradox YAML, include their statuses, such as AI translated or AI reviewed, in the export status selection. ParaTranz JSON exports translations and statuses regardless of these checkboxes.
settings.title: App Settings
settings.description: Configure the display language, appearance, AI services, translation models, and shortcuts.
settings.open.title: Open settings and save changes
settings.open.body: Open Settings from the main window. Select a category in the tree on the left to display its options on the right. App, Translation, and Files also contain subcategories.
settings.buttons.name: Button
settings.buttons.save.label: Save
settings.buttons.save.body: Validate and save changes, then close settings.
settings.buttons.apply.label: Apply
settings.buttons.apply.body: Validate and save changes while keeping settings open for further adjustments.
settings.buttons.cancel.label: Cancel
settings.buttons.cancel.body: Close settings. Changes saved with Apply are not undone. Some operations, including glossary edits, are saved separately.
settings.open.validation: Saving may validate input or test AI model connections. If an error appears, correct the indicated category. If asked to disable unavailable models and save, check the model names before choosing.
settings.application.title: App: language, appearance, and input
settings.application.body: Change how the app looks and accepts input. The display language is separate from a project's target language.
settings.application.language.label: App → UI language
settings.application.language.body: Choose the language used in menus and screens, then click Apply or Save. System default follows your operating system. The self-translation feature on this page lets you create a new interface translation.
settings.application.appearance.label: App → Appearance
settings.application.appearance.body: Choose a Theme and Icon set, then click Apply to check the result. Icon size adjusts the theme and icon preview sizes on this settings page.
settings.application.input.label: App → Input
settings.application.input.body: Choose a Voice input method. Options depend on loaded voice input plugins. Select None if you do not use voice input. For unavailable options, check the environment and plugin status.
settings.shortcuts.title: App → Keyboard shortcuts
settings.shortcuts.body: Choose the Set to edit, or create another with New set. Search by action, location, key, or scope. Select a command and use Add key, Change, or Delete to edit its bindings.
settings.shortcuts.conflicts: If keys conflict, check Conflicting shortcuts. Use Go to conflict to inspect the other action or Replace to change the binding. Resolve conflicts before saving. Restore defaults resets the standard bindings.
settings.ai.title: Translation → AI: register providers and models
settings.ai.body: Register services and models under AI first, then choose the models used for translation under Translation. You can configure multiple providers.
settings.ai.auth.label: Provider and authentication
settings.ai.auth.body: Select a Provider and enter an API key. Some providers show dedicated settings, such as account sign-in, instead of an API key. Follow the instructions on that screen.
settings.ai.models.label: Register models
settings.ai.models.body: Under Models, check model names and whether they are enabled. Use Add model for more models. Reset to default models restores the selected provider's default list. Providers with dedicated settings may show different options.
settings.ai.test.label: Connection test
settings.ai.test.body: Click Connection test to check enabled models. If a test fails, check the credentials and model name. Hover over each model row for details.
settings.translation.title: Translation: choose models and concurrency
settings.translation.body: Assign models registered under AI to translation tasks.
settings.translation.models.label: High model and Low model
settings.translation.models.body: Select a model for each. Both are required; you may use different models or the same model. If a model is missing, check its registration and enabled state under AI.
settings.translation.range.label: Low model range
settings.translation.range.body: Adjust the slider from Narrow to Wide. This changes which entries use the low model based on differences or similarity to reference translations. The current conditions appear below the slider.
settings.translation.concurrency.label: Concurrent requests
settings.translation.concurrency.body: Set how many requests are sent to AI at once. Adjust this to your service limits and processing conditions.
settings.terms.title: Translation → Tone and Glossary
settings.terms.tone.label: Tone
settings.terms.tone.body: Select a tone and edit its name and instruction prompt. Conditional tones support branches and conditions, evaluated from top to bottom. Save with Apply or Save in settings.
settings.terms.glossary.label: Glossary
settings.terms.glossary.body: Choose a game and glossary, then check the source and target languages. Add, edit, or delete terms and manage source terms, preferred translations, variants, and notes. Use search to filter terms.
settings.terms.immediate: Glossary changes are saved immediately. Cancel in settings does not undo them.
settings.rules.title: Translation → Exclusion rules
settings.rules.body: Use regular expressions to specify tags to preserve without translation for each game. Display control tags control features such as colors and line breaks. Display content tags expand into names, numbers, icons, and similar content.
settings.rules.edit: Select a Game and use Add rule to set the enabled state, tag category, regular expression, and example. Select and delete unneeded rules. Restore defaults for this game resets its rules. Fix any indicated regular expression errors before saving.
settings.files.title: Files → Source folder monitoring
settings.files.body: Configure detection of changes to source folders. Use Add watch target and check each target's settings. Start monitoring and Stop monitoring control monitoring; apply the settings afterward.
settings.files.watch: Check monitoring status, target count, error count, and pending updates. Use Review updates for changes or View details for errors.
settings.files.pending: In the current implementation, automatic saving, backups, encoding preservation, and line ending preservation directly under Files, and text size and list wrapping under Appearance, are not saved or applied even if changed in settings.
settings.integration.title: MCP and plugins
settings.integration.mcp.label: App → MCP: connect to the app
settings.integration.mcp.body: To control the app from an external tool, enable MCP connections to the app, configure the port, connection token, and exposed operations (read, edit, translate, export), then apply. Check Connection status and use Copy connection info to obtain the details for the external tool.
settings.integration.resources.label: App → MCP: connect to external resources
settings.integration.resources.body: Add, edit, or delete external MCP connections under External resources. Choose Local process or HTTP, enter the endpoint and required information, then use Check connection.
settings.integration.plugins.label: Plugins
settings.integration.plugins.body: Select a plugin under Plugins in the left tree. Pages and options depend on the loaded plugins.
projects.title: Managing Projects
projects.description: Save and resume translation work, manage target languages, and handle source updates.
projects.about.title: What is a project?
projects.about.body: A project manages source text and translation work together in an .alproj file. Opening it restores source text and translations from that file; it does not reread the game translation data imported during creation. Original file and folder locations are also recorded so updates can be imported later.
projects.about.export: Save the project to resume your work later. Use Export translations separately to create files for games or other tools.
projects.save.title: Save and Save as
projects.save.body: Choose File → Save project. On the first save, choose a location and filename with the .alproj extension. A message at the bottom confirms that the project was saved. Later saves use the same file.
projects.save.as: To keep an earlier version of your work, choose Save project as… and specify another name or location. After saving successfully, Save project uses the new file.
projects.open.title: Open a saved project
projects.open.file.label: Choose a file
projects.open.file.body: Choose File → Open project… and select an .alproj file. Once loading finishes, the saved source text, translations, and statuses for each language are restored.
projects.open.recent.label: Open a recent project
projects.open.recent.body: Recent projects on the Create project screen lists up to 20 saved or opened projects. Check the name and path, then double-click an entry to resume. If you moved the file, use Open project… to select its new location.
projects.open.note: The current implementation requires the file format reader plugin used when importing the source. For example, a project imported from Paradox YAML needs that reader. It reclassifies the source after restoration from .alproj. If no project reader is available, check that the original import plugin is enabled and available.
projects.languages.title: Manage target languages
projects.languages.body: A project can contain multiple target languages. Source text is shared; translations and statuses have separate workspaces for each language.
projects.languages.add.label: Add a language
projects.languages.add.body: Open Add language and search the language list by name or code. Click Add on the desired row, then Close. The new workspace starts untranslated.
projects.languages.custom.label: Use a language that is not listed
projects.languages.custom.body: On the Custom language tab, enter a Display name and Language code, then click Register and add. The language is registered in the app and a workspace is added to this project. For an already registered code, use the language list.
projects.languages.switch.label: Switch the working language
projects.languages.switch.body: Choose a Target language in the main window. Translations, statuses, glossary, and tone switch to that language's settings. Switching clears search and sets the status filter to Untranslated. Select All or another filter to see translated entries.
projects.languages.remove.label: Remove a language
projects.languages.remove.body: Open Add language and click the remove button on an added language's row. Confirming removes that language's translations and statuses. Shared source text and other language workspaces remain. Save the project under another name first if you need to preserve those translations.
projects.languages.save: Save the project after adding or removing languages or changing output slots. Output slots are configured per language and are separate from the target language itself.
projects.updates.title: Import source updates
projects.updates.prepare: When the source changes, reload data from the recorded folder and compare it with the project. Currently, you must register a target and enable Source folder monitoring under Settings → Files. When changes are detected, Review updates appears in the main window. Click it or choose File → Check source updates….
projects.updates.compare: In Review updates, switch between Added, Changed, and Deleted, select an entry, and compare Before and After. Click Apply updates to import the changes or Review later to postpone.
projects.updates.add.label: Added
projects.updates.add.body: New entries are added as untranslated to every language workspace.
projects.updates.change.label: Changed
projects.updates.change.body: Translations and statuses for the same entry ID are retained and marked Source updated — review required. This includes changes to source text or context.
projects.updates.remove.label: Deleted
projects.updates.remove.body: Entries removed from the source are removed from all language workspaces, together with their translations and statuses.
projects.updates.review: After applying updates, filter by Source updated — review required and check that translations still match the new source. Find new entries under Untranslated and translate them. Do this for each target language.
projects.updates.save: If the project already has a save path, applying updates also saves its .alproj file. Use Save as before applying if you want to keep the earlier state. If the source changes again during review, you must review the differences again.
projects.switch.title: Switch projects or finish work
projects.switch.body: Use Open project… to resume another project, or File → New project… to open Create project. Opening this screen alone does not discard the current project; switching happens after a new project is created. Save the project before finishing work.
projects.switch.unsaved: If you have unsaved changes when switching projects or closing the app, you are asked whether to save. Choose Save to keep your work, Discard to proceed without it, or Cancel to stay.
translation.title: Translating, Editing, and Reviewing
translation.description: Select entries, translate with AI or edit manually, confirm translations, and track review work using statuses.
translation.views.title: Choose a language and view
translation.views.body: Open a project and choose the Target language at the top. Use Add language if needed. Translation and editing apply to the selected language's workspace.
translation.views.list.label: List
translation.views.list.body: View keys, source text, translations, statuses, and files in a table. Use Translate on a row for AI translation, or double-click a translation cell to edit it. Right-click a column heading to change visible columns and their order.
translation.views.focus.label: Focus
translation.views.focus.body: Review and edit one entry at a time with larger source and translation fields. Select an entry in the list on the left or use Previous and Next. Page controls and Entries per page change the displayed range.
translation.search.title: Find entries with search and status filters
translation.search.body: Combine the search field and status filter at the top. Use Untranslated for entries awaiting translation, Unconfirmed for edits in progress, or Source updated — review required for changed sources. Choose All to include translated entries.
translation.search.syntax: Search supports key:, source:, target:, context:, file:, and status:. For example, file:dialogue.json AND source:magic finds source text containing “magic” in that file. Combine conditions with AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses. Buttons beside the search field toggle case sensitivity, whole-word matching, and regular expressions.
translation.search.note: Entries can disappear from the current filter when translation or confirmation changes their status. Clear search and choose All if you cannot find an entry.
translation.ai.title: Translate with AI
translation.ai.single.label: Translate the current entry
translation.ai.single.body: Click Translate on a list row or AI translation in Focus view. Translation uses your high and low models, tone, glossary, and other settings.
translation.ai.selected.label: Translate selected rows
translation.ai.selected.body: Select rows to show ▶ Translate selected (count) at the top. Click it to translate those entries. If translated or unconfirmed entries are included, choose whether to overwrite with new translations or translate only untranslated entries.
translation.ai.all.label: Translate all untranslated entries
translation.ai.all.body: Clear the row selection and click ▶ Translate all. It targets untranslated entries in the current target language, regardless of search or status filters. Select rows first if you want to limit the scope.
translation.ai.stop: During processing, the top button changes to Stop. Click it or choose Translation → Stop to interrupt. Progress and final success/failure counts appear at the bottom. If entries fail, check the errors and AI settings before retrying them.
translation.ai.exclusions: AI translation skips empty sources, locked or hidden entries, entries with unconfirmed edits, entries being translated, and entries excluded by rules. Confirm or revert unconfirmed edits before retranslating them.
translation.models.title: Compare translations from multiple models
translation.models.body: Click Translate with all models in Focus view or the menu beside a row's Translate button. Opening the screen starts translating the current source with each enabled registered model. Click Use this translation on the preferred result to apply it to the entry with AI translated status.
translation.edit.title: Edit and confirm translations
translation.edit.body: Edit a translation cell in List view or the Translation field in Focus view. Copy source in Focus view puts the source text in the translation field. Edits are marked Unconfirmed.
translation.edit.confirm: Finishing cell editing in List view or clicking Save in Focus view opens Confirm translation. Compare the source and translation, choose a tone, and click Confirm. Choose Back to editing to continue. Register any missing individual tone in Settings → Tone first.
translation.edit.save.label: Choose how to save
translation.edit.save.body: The Save menu in Focus view offers Save and next (human translation), Save (stay), and saves with specific statuses. Use Save as human review after reviewing a translation. Without an explicit status, confirmed manual edits normally become Human translated; empty translations become Untranslated.
translation.edit.revert.label: Discard unconfirmed edits
translation.edit.revert.body: Click Revert in Focus view or right-click a list row and choose Revert. This discards unconfirmed edits and restores the last confirmed translation; it does not undo earlier confirmed versions.
translation.edit.project: Confirming translations and saving the .alproj file are separate operations. Also use File → Save project to preserve your work.
translation.states.title: Use statuses to track review work
translation.states.body: Choose a status in the list or specify one in the Focus view Save menu. Manual status changes also ask you to select a tone in Confirm translation. Filter by status at the top to track remaining work.
translation.states.name: Status or marker
translation.states.untranslated.label: Untranslated
translation.states.untranslated.body: Entries awaiting translation. Included in Translate all.
translation.states.translated.label: AI translated / Human translated
translation.states.translated.body: A translation has been created. Compare it with the source and edit or review as needed.
translation.states.reviewed.label: AI reviewed / Human reviewed
translation.states.reviewed.body: The translation has been reviewed. Use Save as human review to record completed human review.
translation.states.pending.label: Unconfirmed
translation.states.pending.body: Edits have been made since the last confirmation. Confirm the translation or discard edits with Revert.
translation.states.doubtful.label: Doubtful
translation.states.doubtful.body: Mark translations whose wording or meaning needs further consideration. Filter by this status to revisit them later.
translation.states.protected.label: Locked / Hidden
translation.states.protected.body: Excluded from AI translation and bulk replacement. Choose Locked or Hidden in the status filter to find them.
translation.states.errors.label: Translation error / Review error / Review issues
translation.states.errors.body: Indicates a processing failure or review findings. Check the source, translation, and reported error or issue.
translation.shared.title: Reuse translations for identical or similar entries
translation.shared.exact: After confirmation or AI translation, Apply to exact matches may appear. Check the target statuses and counts, then choose Apply or Do not apply. Manually confirmed translations produce Human translated entries; AI results produce AI translated entries.
translation.shared.similar: If AI translation of similar entries appears, check the reference translation, statuses, and counts, then choose Translate with AI or Do not translate. AI creates a translation for each similar entry using the reference. Results are marked AI translated.
translation.replace.title: Find and replace translation text
translation.replace.body: Expand the replacement field using the button to the left of search, then enter the search and replacement text. Replacement supports plain text or a single translation condition such as target:word. Compound conditions using AND or conditions targeting only source text cannot be used for replacement.
translation.replace.scope: Replace changes the first match in the current entry's translation. Replace all changes every match in translations in the current filtered results. Locked, hidden, or currently translating entries are excluded. Regular expression replacements support references such as \1 and \g<name>.
translation.replace.pending: Replaced translations become unconfirmed. Filter by Unconfirmed, review them, and confirm.
translation.review.title: Review tools
translation.review.ai.label: Review in the AI settings panel
translation.review.ai.body: Open View → AI settings panel and enable AI review after translation, then select a Review model. You can also check the tone and glossary in this panel.
translation.review.display.label: Text display settings
translation.review.display.body: Use Text display settings near search and status to toggle displaying newline markers as line breaks, coloring translation tags, and rendering color tags as actual colors. Available options depend on file format and plugin support.
translation.review.problems.label: Problems
translation.review.problems.body: Open Help → Problems to view issue types, affected entries, details, and filenames. Jump to location is not supported in the current implementation. Use the entry details or filename to find it with main-window search.
translation.review.finish: Save the project after reviewing. To create translation files, open Export translations and check the output folder and format settings. For Paradox YAML and similar formats, select the statuses to include. ParaTranz JSON exports translations and statuses as they are.
glossaryTone.title: Glossaries and Tone
glossaryTone.description: Register preferred names, terminology, and writing styles for translation. Learn about nested glossaries, JSON import/export, and conditional tone selection.
glossaryTone.open.title: Manage settings and apply them to translation
glossaryTone.open.body: Manage glossaries and tones under Settings → Translation → Glossary or Tone. You can also open View → AI settings panel and choose Manage glossaries… or Manage tones….
glossaryTone.open.apply: To use a glossary or tone for AI translation, close settings and select it under Glossary to use or Tone in the AI settings panel. Selecting something to edit in settings does not select it for translation.
glossaryTone.glossary.title: Choose a game and languages, then create a glossary
glossaryTone.glossary.languages: Choose a Game in glossary settings. The root of the left tree is the game's shared glossary. On first use, select it and set two different languages for Source and Translation. Child glossaries inherit this pair. Swap reverses their direction for display.
glossaryTone.glossary.create: Register common terms at the root. To organize by purpose, select a parent glossary, click the add button for glossaries, and enter a name. The new glossary is created beneath the selected one. Rename it in the tree or with the right-click Rename command.
glossaryTone.glossary.save: Glossary creation, renaming, language settings, and term changes are saved immediately; Cancel in settings does not undo them. Once terms exist, you cannot switch to a different language pair. Use Swap to reverse the existing pair.
glossaryTone.terms.title: Add, edit, and search terms
glossaryTone.terms.add: Check the glossary and source/translation direction, then click Add term. Enter the part of speech, source term, and preferred translation, then save. For example, for English to Japanese, enter “Iron Guard” with the preferred translation “鉄衛隊”. Select Edit on an existing row or double-click it to open it.
glossaryTone.terms.variants.label: Source variants and translation variants
glossaryTone.terms.variants.body: Register alternative spellings or inflected forms of the same term. Enter a string and press Enter or the add button. Source variants also help find terms in source text. Select and remove unneeded variants.
glossaryTone.terms.case.label: Case sensitivity
glossaryTone.terms.case.body: Set case sensitivity separately for source and translation. The source setting is used when matching glossary terms for AI translation.
glossaryTone.terms.memo.label: Notes
glossaryTone.terms.memo.body: Record cautions and review points, such as when to use a translation or the reason for a decision, for future editors.
glossaryTone.terms.search: Search glossaries filters the left tree by name. Term search supports source:, target:, variant: (variants in either language), and memo:. Combine conditions, for example source:magic AND NOT memo:review.
glossaryTone.inheritance.title: Inherit parent terms and override them in children
glossaryTone.inheritance.body: A child glossary shows inherited parent terms and its own terms. For example, keep common game terms in the parent and mod-specific translations in a child. Selecting the child for translation also uses inherited terms.
glossaryTone.inheritance.edit: Inherited terms appear in a lighter color; hover to see their origin. Editing and saving one in a child creates an override without changing the parent. Deleting the override restores the inherited term. To delete the original term itself, select the parent glossary.
glossaryTone.inheritance.delete: Delete term affects terms registered in the selected glossary. Deleting a glossary also deletes its own terms. The game's shared glossary and glossaries with children cannot be deleted.
glossaryTone.import.title: Import glossary JSON
glossaryTone.import.body: Select the destination glossary and drop one JSON file onto the import area, or click Choose file. In Import glossary, choose a Format and check the filename, destination, and contents. For external formats, also check the source/translation direction.
glossaryTone.import.merge.label: Merge into the selected glossary
glossaryTone.import.merge.body: Import terms into the selected glossary. AUTOlingua2 format updates information in both languages for matching terms. External formats preserve existing main expressions, variants, and case settings while merging expressions and notes. The dialog also explains the behavior.
glossaryTone.import.new.label: Create beneath the selected glossary
glossaryTone.import.new.body: Create a new child glossary without changing existing terms. Files containing parent-child relationships preserve that structure.
glossaryTone.import.note: Glossaries containing parent-child relationships cannot be merged into an existing glossary. Check the contents, click Import, and review the created, added, and updated counts. For ParaTranz glossary JSON, choose ParaTranz glossary as the format.
glossaryTone.export.title: Export a glossary
glossaryTone.export.body: Select a glossary and click Export…. Choose the Format and export mode, check the current structure and output contents, then click Export… again to choose a JSON save path. Also check the language direction for external formats.
glossaryTone.export.own.label: Selected glossary only: own terms
glossaryTone.export.own.body: Export terms registered directly in the selected glossary, excluding inherited parent terms.
glossaryTone.export.flat.label: Selected glossary only: merge inheritance
glossaryTone.export.flat.body: Combine inherited parent terms and child overrides into one glossary containing the effective terms of the selected glossary.
glossaryTone.export.tree.label: Selected glossary with ancestors or the full inheritance tree
glossaryTone.export.tree.body: AUTOlingua2 format can include the selected glossary and its parents or the entire inheritance tree. External formats offer own terms only or merged inheritance.
glossaryTone.paratranz.title: Use ParaTranz glossaries
glossaryTone.paratranz.import: Choose ParaTranz glossary as the import format. First configure the two languages at the destination's root and check the displayed source/translation direction. Translation JSON and glossary JSON are different formats.
glossaryTone.paratranz.merge: Import source terms, preferred translations, source variants, parts of speech, and notes. Supported parts of speech are noun, verb, adjective, and adverb. Multiple source expressions with the same translation and part of speech may be combined as variants of one term. Check the file and merged-variant counts before importing.
glossaryTone.paratranz.export: Choose ParaTranz glossary for export as well. Check the language direction and choose own terms or merged inheritance, then review and save. To share all effective terms for a game or mod, select a child glossary and merge inheritance.
glossaryTone.paratranz.omitted: ParaTranz format does not export translation variants, case settings, or glossary hierarchy. The export screen shows counts of omitted information. Use AUTOlingua2 glossary format to preserve these details.
glossaryTone.tone.title: Create a normal tone
glossaryTone.tone.create: In tone settings, choose the option to create a new tone. Set Type to Normal tone and enter a Tone name and Instruction prompt. To edit an existing tone, search for and select it in the tone selector.
glossaryTone.tone.example: For example, name the tone “Polite Japanese” and use “Translate using polite desu/masu forms.” Describe the required style clearly for narrative, dialogue, or other text.
glossaryTone.tone.save: Save tone changes with Apply or Save. Fix empty names or prompts and condition errors before saving. Deleting a normal tone changes references to it in conditional tones to None.
glossaryTone.conditions.title: Select tones automatically with conditions
glossaryTone.conditions.create: Register the normal tones you want to use first. Create a new tone, set Type to Conditional tone, and enter a name. Add an If branch, then set its condition and the tone to use.
glossaryTone.conditions.edit: Conditions can inspect Filename, Key, or Source using Equals, Contains, Starts with, Ends with, or Regular expression search. Enter the comparison text and select a normal tone. Branches are evaluated from top to bottom; the first match is used. Also set the final Else tone. None adds no tone instruction for that branch.
glossaryTone.conditions.example: For example, use Polite Japanese when Key starts with dialogue_, and Plain Japanese otherwise. AI translation selects the normal tone based on these conditions. Condition strings are case-sensitive.
glossaryTone.conditions.advanced: Combine conditions with AND (all), OR (any), or NOT (does not match). Use Add group to group conditions, and move buttons to reorder branches. You can nest conditions inside a branch, but nesting five or more levels is discouraged. Check the condition preview and errors before saving.
glossaryTone.use.title: Choose the glossary and tone for translation
glossaryTone.use.select: After configuration, check the Target language and select a Glossary to use and Tone in the AI settings panel. Glossaries come from the current game. Child glossaries include inherited terms. Choose None to disable either feature. Selections are retained per target language, so check them after switching languages.
glossaryTone.use.effect: Normal AI translation matches registered terms and source variants in the source text and sends the matching source terms and preferred translations to AI. Tone instructions come from the normal tone or the normal tone selected by conditions. Changing definitions or selections does not automatically rewrite existing translations. Retranslate or edit entries as needed.
glossaryTone.use.confirm: When confirming manual edits, select the normal tone actually used for that translation, rather than a conditional tone. Also save the project afterward. Glossary and tone definitions are managed separately by the app; the project records which glossary and tone are selected.
export.title: Exporting Translation Files
export.description: Export translations as Paradox YAML, ParaTranz JSON, or a character list for BMFont.
export.before.title: Before exporting
export.before.body: Export creates files for games or other tools. It is separate from saving an .alproj file to resume work, so also save the project. Export uses data in the project and does not reread the original imported files.
export.before.scope: Export includes every target language in the project. It is not limited to the current language, selected rows, or search/status filters. If no target languages exist, use Add language to create a workspace.
export.before.pending: Unconfirmed edits are not exported; the last confirmed translations are used. To include your latest edits, filter by Unconfirmed and confirm them first.
export.destination.title: 1. Open export and choose a destination
export.destination.open: Choose File → Export translations…. Select a folder in the export screen and check the Output folder field at the bottom. You can also type a folder path directly there.
export.destination.navigate: Navigate with the folder tree on the left or folder list in the center. Single-click a folder to select it as the destination; double-click to open it. Use Back, Forward, or Up as well. You can enter a path through Location → Enter path and press Enter, or use New folder.
export.destination.existing: Choose an existing destination folder. If an output file already exists with the same name, export reports an error instead of overwriting it. For another export, use New folder or another destination to keep outputs separate.
export.format.title: 2. Choose an export method
export.format.body: Select a format under Export method. Format-specific options appear under Export settings. The status selection and export settings sections can be expanded or collapsed with their heading buttons.
export.format.name: Export method
export.format.yaml.label: Paradox YAML (*.yml)
export.format.yaml.body: Create YAML translation files for games. Configure folder layout and, for EU4, encoding.
export.format.json.label: ParaTranz JSON (*.json)
export.format.json.body: Exchange source text, translations, keys, context, and statuses in ParaTranz translation format. Export glossary JSON from the glossary settings described in chapter 6.
export.format.bmfont.label: BMFont character list (*.txt)
export.format.bmfont.body: Create a text file listing unique characters used in the text, for selecting characters during font creation.
export.states.title: 3. Choose which translation statuses to use
export.states.body: Paradox YAML and translated-text BMFont exports use translations whose statuses are checked. AI translated, Human translated, AI reviewed, Human reviewed, and Locked are selected by default. Narrow this selection if you only want reviewed translations, for example.
export.states.fallback: Entries with unchecked statuses or empty translations use the source text instead. This setting does not remove entries from files. For example, unchecking Doubtful exports the source rather than the doubtful translation.
export.states.exchange: ParaTranz JSON exports confirmed translations and statuses regardless of these checkboxes and does not substitute source text for untranslated entries. BMFont's Source option is also unaffected by the status selection.
export.yaml.title: Paradox YAML settings
export.yaml.slot: Before exporting, switch through target languages in the main window and check each Output slot. The target language determines the translation language; the output slot determines the game's language slot. YAML headers, filenames, and language folders use the output slot.
export.yaml.layout.label: Folder layout
export.yaml.layout.body: Separate folders by language creates folders based on output slots. Same folder omits that language folder. If the original path contains localisation or localization, the structure below it is used. A localization folder is created beneath the destination for CK3 and Victoria 3; other games use localisation.
export.yaml.encoding.label: Encoding (EU4)
export.yaml.encoding.body: For EU4, choose UTF-8 with BOM or EU4 CJK escape. EU4 CJK escape is selected initially if any target language is Japanese, Chinese, or Korean. Check compatibility with your game environment. Other games use UTF-8 with BOM.
export.yaml.files: A .yml file is created for each source file. The language suffix in its filename follows the output slot. Multiple targets using the same output slot may create duplicate paths; check each language's slot if this happens.
export.json.title: Exchange translations and statuses with ParaTranz JSON
export.json.body: JSON files follow the source file structure within a folder for each target language code. Each entry contains key, original, translation, context, and a stage representing its status. Non-.json source filenames have .json appended. App statuses map to ParaTranz as follows.
export.json.untranslated.label: Untranslated / Translation error / Review error
export.json.translated.label: AI translated / Human translated
export.json.reviewed.label: AI reviewed / Human reviewed
export.json.doubtful.label: Doubtful / Review issues
export.json.locked.label: Locked
export.json.locked.body: Locked (已锁定, stage 9). Only ParaTranz administrators can unlock it, and its translation is used in generated translation files.
export.json.hidden.label: Hidden
export.json.hidden.body: Hidden (已隐藏, stage -1). ParaTranz uses the source text in generated translation files.
export.json.reviewNote: ParaTranz also has a Reviewed status (已审核 / 二校, stage 5) after Checked. Both AI reviewed and Human reviewed in this app export as Checked (stage 3). The distinction between AI and human work is not retained in ParaTranz statuses.
export.bmfont.title: Create a BMFont character list
export.bmfont.body: In Export settings → Target text, choose Translation or Source. The output is one line of unique characters sorted by Unicode, with whitespace, line breaks, and some control characters removed, encoded as UTF-8 with BOM. This feature does not create font images or font files.
export.bmfont.files: With one target language, the file is characters.txt. For translations in multiple languages, characters_LANGUAGE.txt is created for each language, using its output slot if set, otherwise its target language code. Source text with multiple languages produces a combined characters_source.txt. Translation mode also includes source characters for entries outside the selected statuses.
export.run.title: 4. Export and check the files
export.run.body: Check the destination, method, statuses, and format settings, then click Export. The current filename appears during processing. When finished, inspect the files and folder structure before using them in your game or receiving tool.
export.run.errors: If duplicate filenames or paths are reported, check the destination and each language's output slot. Cancellation or write errors may leave files already created. Check the output contents and choose another folder before retrying.
aiChat.title: AI Chat
aiChat.description: Ask AI about source text and translations, request searches, edits, and reviews, and control scope and proposed changes.
aiChat.start.title: Open AI chat and send a message
aiChat.start.open: Open a project and choose View → AI chat. Use the model button at the bottom of chat to select a service and model. Models enabled under Settings → AI appear as options.
aiChat.start.send: Type a question or request and click Send or press Enter. Use Shift+Enter for a line break. Specify the target language, entries, and whether you want advice or actual changes.
aiChat.start.model: Use a model that supports chat. If no model can be selected, check registration and enabled states under Settings → AI. You cannot change models during a response or voice input.
aiChat.references.title: Attach translation entries as references
aiChat.references.rows: Select list rows, right-click, and choose Insert into chat to add references to the input. You can also drag rows into it. References contain entry IDs, keys, source text, translations, and whether entries are untranslated.
aiChat.references.inspect: Click an inserted reference to inspect what will be sent. Add a request such as “Explain whether this translation matches the source meaning.” References in the input can be selected and deleted like text.
aiChat.references.snapshot: References capture the content at the time of insertion. Later edits do not update earlier references. Insert a new reference or ask AI to inspect the current entry for the latest state.
aiChat.attachments.title: Attach images or text files
aiChat.attachments.body: Use Attach images/files or drop local files into the input. Attach reference text or images and explain which details AI should use.
aiChat.attachments.images.label: Images
aiChat.attachments.images.body: PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF are supported, up to 5,000,000 bytes per file. Your AI must support the image format. Reduce the number of images if the combined size is too large.
aiChat.attachments.text.label: Text files
aiChat.attachments.text.body: Use UTF-8 or Unicode text with a BOM, up to 800,000 bytes and 200,000 characters. PDF and Word documents cannot be read directly; attach the required content as text.
aiChat.options.title: Choose scope and execution mode
aiChat.options.open: Open Scope and execution at the top of chat and check the operation scope and execution mode before sending a request.
aiChat.options.project.label: Entire project
aiChat.options.project.body: Work across the project. If it has multiple languages, specify which target language to use in your request.
aiChat.options.file.label: Current file
aiChat.options.file.body: Use the current entry's source file and active target language. First select an entry from the desired file in List or Focus view.
aiChat.options.selection.label: Selected rows
aiChat.options.selection.body: Use selected rows in List view or the current entry in Focus view. Select entries before sending if there is no target.
aiChat.options.confirm.label: Review proposals
aiChat.options.confirm.body: Review changes before applying them. Proposals appear in chat, where you can select which ones to apply. This is the default mode.
aiChat.options.direct.label: Execute as requested
aiChat.options.direct.body: Execute requested operations without a proposal review step. Check the scope, language, and requested changes before sending. Results appear in operation and task displays in chat.
aiChat.options.references: Attached references and operation scope are separate. Even if you intend to modify only previously attached rows, check the current selection and scope.
aiChat.requests.title: Example requests
aiChat.requests.body: State the target and purpose clearly, as in these examples.
aiChat.requests.consult.label: Discuss wording
aiChat.requests.consult.body: “Explain differences in meaning between the attached translation and source, and suggest natural alternatives. Do not change anything yet.”
aiChat.requests.find.label: Find and select entries
aiChat.requests.find.body: “Find Japanese translations containing 鉄衛隊 and select the matching rows on screen.” Retrieving search results and selecting them in the UI are separate, so ask explicitly if you want them selected.
aiChat.requests.edit.label: Revise translations
aiChat.requests.edit.body: “Revise the selected Japanese translations into polite desu/masu style without changing their meaning. I want to review the proposals.” Before sending, set scope to Selected rows and mode to Review proposals.
aiChat.requests.review.label: Request review or term extraction
aiChat.requests.review.body: Ask “Check the selected Japanese translations for omissions and inconsistent terminology” or “Suggest terms from this file to add to the glossary.” If a review or extraction task starts, check its progress and results.
aiChat.requests.other: You can also request glossary or tone changes, translation, source update checks, project saving, and translation export. Specify required details such as paths and formats. To consult external resources, first register their connection in Settings → MCP.
aiChat.changes.title: Review and apply proposed changes
aiChat.changes.compare: In Review proposals mode, proposed operations appear as Awaiting confirmation in chat. Compare Current and Proposed for each item and check those you want to accept. Select all selects them together; Show target displays the corresponding translation entries.
aiChat.changes.apply: Click Apply selected changes to apply your selection, or Discard to reject proposals. Verify that the operation status becomes Applied and check the actual translations rather than relying only on AI's explanation.
aiChat.changes.undo: Reversible operations show Undo changes. This may fail if subsequent edits conflict; check the reported error. If a proposal is stale because the target changed, ask AI to recreate it using the latest content.
aiChat.changes.save: Save the project afterward to preserve translation changes. Glossary and tone changes made through chat also update their respective management data.
aiChat.progress.title: Inspect results and stop tasks
aiChat.progress.body: Translation, review, and export tasks show progress and status in chat. Click Show results to inspect them. If a task fails, check the error and correct the scope or settings before retrying.
aiChat.progress.stop: During a response, Send becomes Stop. This stops the AI response, but tasks already started may continue. To stop a task too, click Cancel in its task display. Stopping the response does not undo applied changes.
aiChat.voice.title: Dictate a request
aiChat.voice.body: Choose a voice input method under Settings → App → Input. When available, Open voice input appears in chat. With recording methods, click again to stop recording and start recognition. Recognized text is inserted into the input; check and edit it before sending. Chat cannot be sent during voice input or recognition.
aiChat.conversation.title: Read responses and manage conversations
aiChat.conversation.display: Use Copy on a response to copy its text. Markdown source switches the display format. If new results arrive while you are reading older messages, use Latest to return to the bottom.
aiChat.conversation.new: Click New conversation to change topics. The conversation and input are cleared, but pending operations and current project tasks are shown again. Opening another project resets the conversation. Chat history is not saved in .alproj.
aiChat.conversation.switch: You can change AI models during a conversation. On the next send, previous messages and references are sent to the new service too. Use New conversation to start without that context. Long conversations are summarized automatically when needed. If asked to reduce reference material, remove attachments or organize the request in a new conversation.
automation.title: Automation and Integrations
automation.description: Run repetitive screen operations with scripts and use MCP to connect external tools and reference resources.
automation.reference.title: Look up scripting specifications
automation.reference.body: A separate reference page covers syntax, types, operators, branches, functions, all 12 built-in functions, and limitations. Refer to it when writing scripts or investigating errors.
scriptReference.title: Scripting Language Reference
scriptReference.description: Syntax, types, control flow, all built-in functions, and runtime limitations for .als automation scripts.
scriptReference.back.title: Return to the automation guide
automation.methods.title: Choose the right method
automation.methods.script.label: Automation scripts
automation.methods.script.body: Describe and run repeated screen operations in a fixed order, such as adding languages. Save scripts as .als files for reuse.
automation.methods.server.label: Control the app from an external tool
automation.methods.server.body: An MCP-compatible external tool can search, edit, translate, save, and export the open project. Enable app connections under Settings → App → MCP.
automation.methods.resources.label: Read external resources from the app
automation.methods.resources.body: Register an MCP connection that exposes resources and consult them from AI chat. Use External resources in the same MCP settings.
automation.script.title: Open and save scripts
automation.script.open: Choose Translation → Automation script…. Initially, a sample adds several target languages and starts translation. Read it and adjust it to your work before running.
automation.script.files: New clears the script; Open loads a saved .als file. Save writes to the current file; Save as writes to another. Files use UTF-8. An asterisk beside the filename indicates unsaved changes. You are asked to save changes before creating a new script, opening another file, or closing the screen.
automation.script.search: The search field at the top searches the script. Navigate between matches, toggle case sensitivity, whole-word matching, or regular expressions, and expand the replacement field for Replace or Replace all. The bottom shows the cursor line, column, and total lines.
automation.example.title: Example: add several target languages
automation.example.before: This example assumes a project is open and Japanese (ja) and Thai (th) have not been added. When changing language codes, use codes from the app's language list.
automation.example.code:
string[] languages = ["ja", "th"]

for string code in languages {
    click("buttonAddLanguage")
    table_row("tableLanguages", code)
    click("buttonAdd")
    click("buttonClose")
}
automation.example.explanation: For each language in the array, open the language dialog, select the row matching its code, add it, and close the dialog. An already added language has no Add button, so the example stops. Check the target languages before running.
automation.example.ids: Targets use widget IDs such as buttonAddLanguage, not visible names. When started with --debug, the index tooltips let you inspect and copy IDs. IDs normally do not appear when launched without this option.
automation.commands.title: All screen operation functions
automation.commands.name: Operation
automation.commands.click.label: click(id [, rowKey])
automation.commands.click.body: Returns void. id and optional rowKey are strings. Identifies and clicks one button. For a button inside a table row, select one row first or specify a row string, for example click("buttonAdd", "ja"). rowKey is only supported for table-row buttons. Hidden or disabled buttons cannot be clicked.
automation.commands.row.label: table_row(id, key)
automation.commands.row.body: Returns void. Both arguments are strings. Selects and scrolls to one row with a cell whose displayed text exactly matches key. Multiple matching cells within the same row are allowed; matches in multiple rows stop execution. Hidden, disabled, or unselectable tables and rows cannot be selected.
automation.commands.combo.label: combo_select(id, text)
automation.commands.combo.body: Returns void. Both arguments are strings. Selects one item whose display name exactly matches text. Stops if the control is disabled, the item is unselectable, or zero or multiple items match. Display names may change with the interface language.
automation.commands.spin.label: spin_set(id, value)
automation.commands.spin.body: Returns void. id is a string; value is int or float. Sets an absolute value in a numeric input. The value must be finite and within the control's range. Integer controls require a value without a fractional part. Disabled or read-only controls cannot be changed.
automation.spec.screen.add.label: spin_add(id, amount)
automation.spec.screen.add.body: Returns void. id is a string; amount is int or float. Adds amount to the current value. The amount must be nonnegative and the result within the control's range. Other requirements are the same as spin_set.
automation.spec.screen.sub.label: spin_sub(id, amount)
automation.spec.screen.sub.body: Returns void. id is a string; amount is int or float. Subtracts amount from the current value. The amount must be nonnegative and the result within the control's range. Negative amounts cannot be used to add.
automation.spec.syntax.title: Language: syntax, names, and literals
automation.spec.syntax.body: .als is the app's own scripting language. Statements run from top to bottom; function bodies run when called. Use whitespace and line breaks for readability, without semicolons. Blocks use { }; arguments and array elements are separated by commas. // starts a comment through the end of the line. Block comments are not supported.
automation.spec.syntax.names: Variable and function names start with a letter (including Japanese characters) or _, followed by letters, underscores, or digits. Names are case-sensitive. Reserved words are string, int, float, bool, void, function, if, else, for, in, return, break, continue, true, and false. Custom functions also cannot reuse built-in screen operation or read function names.
automation.spec.syntax.literals: Strings use double quotes and JSON escapes such as \n, \t, \r, \", \\, and \uXXXX. Literal line breaks within quoted strings are not allowed. Integers are decimal; floats require digits on both sides of a decimal point, such as 3.5. Exponent and hexadecimal notation are unsupported. Negative values use unary -. Booleans are true or false.
automation.spec.syntax.code:
// Strings, numbers, and booleans
string name = "Translation work"
string lines = "Line 1\nLine 2"
int count = -2
float rate = 1.5
bool enabled = true
automation.spec.types.title: Language: types, variables, and arrays
automation.spec.types.body: Types are string, int, float, bool, and their one-dimensional arrays: string[], int[], float[], and bool[]. Declare with type name = value and reassign with name = value. There is no implicit conversion: assigning to float requires 1.0 rather than integer 1. Type conversion functions are not available.
automation.spec.types.initialization: Declarations may omit an initial value, but a value must be assigned before reading. Initialization in an if requires both branches to initialize the variable. An assignment inside a for loop does not establish initialization outside it, because the loop may never execute.
automation.spec.types.arrays: Arrays use [ ] and contain elements of one type. Empty arrays require context such as string[] names = []. Indexes are zero-based ints; negative or out-of-range indexes are errors. Indexing is read-only: elements cannot be assigned, added, or removed. The entire array can be reassigned. Multidimensional arrays and a length function are not available.
automation.spec.operators.title: Language: operators and precedence
automation.spec.operators.body: Array indexing [ ] has the highest precedence, followed by the table from top to bottom. Binary operators at the same level evaluate left to right. Parentheses override the order. Arithmetic and comparisons cannot mix int and float.
automation.spec.operators.unary.label: ! / unary + / unary -
automation.spec.operators.unary.body: ! negates a bool. Unary + and - apply to int or float signs.
automation.spec.operators.product.body: Multiplication, division, and remainder of the same numeric type. Division returns float even for two ints. Remainder supports both int and float.
automation.spec.operators.sum.body: Addition and subtraction of the same numeric type. + concatenates strings. Strings cannot be concatenated with numbers, and arrays cannot be concatenated.
automation.spec.operators.order.body: Compare ints, floats, or strings of the same type and return bool. Strings are compared by character order.
automation.spec.operators.equal.body: Compare values of the same type and return bool. Arrays compare by their elements. Operations without a return value cannot be compared.
automation.spec.operators.and.body: Boolean AND. The right side is not evaluated if the left side is false.
automation.spec.operators.or.body: Boolean OR. The right side is not evaluated if the left side is true.
automation.spec.operators.division: float value = 5 / 2 produces 2.5. int value = 5 / 2 is a type error. Division or remainder by zero and nonfinite results stop execution with an error.
automation.spec.control.title: Language: conditions, loops, and scope
automation.spec.control.if: Branch with if condition { ... }, if condition { ... } else { ... }, or else if. Conditions must be bool; numbers and strings cannot be used directly. Parentheses around conditions are optional.
automation.spec.control.for: for type variable in array { ... } iterates through an array in order. The variable type must match the element type. break exits the innermost loop; continue skips the rest of the current iteration. Both are only valid inside loops.
automation.spec.control.scope: Variables declared in an if branch or for block exist only in that block. Outer variables can be read and reassigned but cannot be redeclared with the same name. Loop variables must also have names distinct from outer variables.
automation.spec.functions.title: Language: custom functions and return values
automation.spec.functions.definition: Define functions with function name(type argument, ...): returnType { ... } at file scope only. Calls may precede definitions. Argument counts and types must match; duplicate function or parameter names are not allowed. Parameters and return values may use array types.
automation.spec.functions.return: Write return and its value on the same line. A void function may use return without a value or reach the end. Non-void functions must return the declared type on every path. return cannot appear outside a function.
automation.spec.functions.scope: Functions cannot access outer variables; pass required values as arguments. Recursion is allowed, with at most 64 nested custom function calls. Function calls may also be standalone statements.
automation.spec.screen.body: The following six functions operate the UI and return void. Pass a widget ID string rather than a display name. Targets must be visible widgets in the active main window or an app dialog. The automation script screen itself cannot be a target.
automation.spec.read.title: All read functions
automation.spec.read.body: The following six functions read UI values. All IDs are strings. Each target must be one visible widget of the appropriate type in the active app screen. Reading is allowed even if a field is disabled or read-only.
automation.spec.read.spin.label: spin_get(id): int / float
automation.spec.read.spin.body: Reads integer controls as int and decimal controls as float. Call it in a context that determines the type, such as an assignment, argument, or return value. For example, first assign int size = spin_get("spinFocusPageSize") to use the result in calculations or comparisons. A mismatch between the control and expected type stops execution at runtime.
automation.spec.read.combo.label: combo_get(id): string
automation.spec.read.combo.body: Returns the display name of the currently selected item. No selection is an error.
automation.spec.read.text.label: text_get(id): string
automation.spec.read.text.body: Returns the content of a single-line input, multiline plain-text field, or text editor. It does not read labels or button names.
automation.spec.read.check.label: check_get(id): bool
automation.spec.read.check.body: Returns true for a checked checkbox and false for an unchecked one. A partially checked three-state checkbox is an error because it cannot be represented as bool.
automation.spec.read.slider.label: slider_get(id): int
automation.spec.read.slider.body: Returns the slider's current value as int.
automation.spec.read.row.label: table_row_get(id, column): string
automation.spec.read.row.body: column is a nonnegative int. Returns the displayed string in the specified column of the single selected row. No selection, multiple selected rows, a hidden row, an out-of-range column, or a non-string value is an error.
automation.spec.limits.title: Runtime limits and errors
automation.spec.limits.wait: The runner waits up to five seconds for initial main-window activation, screen display or switching, and targets to become visible and enabled. Tasks started by the script, such as translation, loading, saving, and export, are awaited until actual completion rather than for a fixed duration. Duplicate target IDs and invalid types or values are errors.
automation.spec.limits.unsupported: There is no while, numeric range generator, sleep, arbitrary wait condition, exception handling, import, external command execution, file I/O, or arbitrary Python execution. There are also no functions to directly set text, checkbox states, or slider values. Built-ins consist of six screen operations and six read functions.
automation.spec.autoWait.title: Automatically wait for each operation
automation.spec.autoWait.body: Write instructions in order; the runner waits until it can continue. After opening a dialog, it waits until the dialog can be operated; after closing one, until the destination screen can be operated. Translation and subsequent AI review, loading, saving, export, all-model translation, and AI chat wait for processing and results to be reflected. If a confirmation screen appears, execution advances to the next instruction that operates it, then waits for processing after the answer. Unrelated periodic updates and background monitors are not awaited.
automation.spec.autoWait.result: A failed or canceled task, including partial entry failures, stops the script without running later instructions. The screen or task being awaited is shown, and Stop in automation interrupts the wait. Stopping does not automatically cancel tasks such as translation that have already started.
automation.spec.limits.syntax.label: Syntax or type error before execution
automation.spec.limits.syntax.body: The entire script is validated before any screen operation. Check the reported line and column for quotes, brackets, types, uninitialized variables, and function arguments or return values. Excessive expression or block nesting is also an error.
automation.spec.limits.target.label: Target cannot be identified
automation.spec.limits.target.body: Check the active screen, widget ID, and visible/enabled state. If multiple widgets, rows, or items match, narrow the target to one. IDs do not allow operating widgets on other screens.
automation.spec.limits.value.label: Invalid value, type, or range
automation.spec.limits.value.body: Check array indexes, table columns, numeric input ranges, integer versus float types, and division by zero. Also check that a read value's type matches its declaration.
automation.spec.limits.active.label: Runtime stop or timeout
automation.spec.limits.active.body: Check initial main-window activation, switching to another app, and detection of manual input. Runtime errors and stops do not undo earlier operations. Inspect completed lines in the log and resume based on the current state.
automation.run.title: Start, inspect results, and stop
automation.run.start: Close other dialogs, prepare the starting screen, and click Start. After syntax validation, the automation window is minimized and execution begins when the main window becomes active. The script cannot be edited while running. Target buttons must be visible and enabled.
automation.run.stop: Click Stop to interrupt. Closing the automation window or manually clicking, typing, or scrolling in the main window or other monitored app screens also stops execution. For errors, inspect the automation status and log line/column, then correct the target ID or screen state.
automation.run.results: Completed appears only after script-started tasks finish. Even if the last instruction translates or saves, completion is awaited automatically. On failure or cancellation, check the responsible instruction and reason. Stopping does not undo completed operations or automatically cancel tasks already started. Also save your work in the project.
automation.server.title: Connect external tools to the app with MCP
automation.server.enable: Open Settings → App → MCP and enable MCP connections to the app. Set Port to Automatic or a chosen number, check the connection token and exposed operations, then click Apply or Save.
automation.server.connect: When a URL appears under Connection status, click Copy connection info. Register that URL and Authorization: Bearer credentials in the external tool's MCP settings. The app accepts Streamable HTTP connections on 127.0.0.1 on the same computer. Keep the app running.
automation.server.read.label: Read
automation.server.read.body: Retrieve and search project information, source files, translation entries, and similar data.
automation.server.edit.label: Edit
automation.server.edit.body: Change translations, glossaries, tones, and language settings, apply source updates, and save projects.
automation.server.translate.label: Translate
automation.server.translate.body: Run translation, AI review, and term candidate extraction.
automation.server.export.label: Export
automation.server.export.body: Preview output and export translation files.
automation.results.title: Check results of externally requested operations
automation.results.proposals: Check execution mode in AI chat → Scope and execution. In Review proposals mode, changes await confirmation and appear as proposals in AI chat. Compare Current and Proposed, select the desired items, and click Apply selected changes. Execute as requested applies changes directly.
automation.results.jobs: Check progress, results, and errors for tasks such as translation and export. In the AI chat task display, use Show results to inspect output and Cancel to stop a running task. Ending the conversation in the external tool does not necessarily stop tasks already started.
automation.results.disable: To disconnect, disable MCP connections to the app and apply. If you regenerate the token or change the port, apply the changes, copy the new connection information, and update the external tool as well.
automation.resources.title: Connect to external reference resources
automation.resources.add: In MCP settings → External resources, click Add. In External MCP connection, enter a name, select the connection method, and fill in the required fields according to the endpoint's instructions. Select existing connections to Edit or Delete them.
automation.resources.local.label: Local process
automation.resources.local.body: Set Executable or MCP URL to the executable to launch and enter one launch argument per line. The app starts the process and reads its resources.
automation.resources.http.label: HTTP
automation.resources.http.body: Set Executable or MCP URL to an HTTP or HTTPS MCP endpoint. Enter a connection token if authentication is required.
automation.resources.check: After adding a connection, select it and click Check connection. Once resource reading succeeds, save it with Apply or Save in settings. Then ask AI chat, for example, “Search the registered resources and check how this term should be translated.”
automation.resources.scope: External resource connections support MCP resource listing, resource templates, and resource reading. Endpoints that do not support resource reading cannot connect. Registering a connection does not enable every operation offered by that endpoint.
